# Arya: full documentation

<!-- https://docs.arya.teamnightshift.org/docs/judges -->

# For judges

Arya is a grocery app that learns how you shop from your receipts and helps shoppers help each other. It puts the whole grocery chore in one place: shared lists, a guided route through the store, a clear view of your spend and usage, and out-of-stock warnings from other shoppers. Every step that needs AI uses a Meta model. The money, timing and list logic is plain code.

This is an Indie track entry. I built it alone in the hackathon window (Oct 27 to Nov 4, 2026). The problem statement is **Build for Your World**: a tool for everyday life that uses Meta's models to read receipts, labels, voice and shelves.

## Start here

- **Demo video (3 min):** [youtu.be/PeWF66ss3oI](https://youtu.be/PeWF66ss3oI). The live demo and the guided path work without it.
- **Try it, no sign-up:** https://arya.teamnightshift.org, then tap "Try it now". It opens a made-up household in a sandbox that exists only for your visit. Use a phone if you can. On a laptop, make the window about 390 px wide. Camera steps need a phone. The 8-minute guided path is [`docs/quest/JUDGE-PLAYBOOK.md`](/docs/quest/judge-playbook), with a [sample receipt photo](/repo/docs/images/sample-receipt.jpg), a [sample shelf photo](/repo/docs/images/sample-shelf.jpg), and a walkthrough video of the same path, with voice and captions (3 min 48 s): [youtu.be/cbJflgCXV5U](https://youtu.be/cbJflgCXV5U).
- **Everything else:** the [README](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md) (what it is, why I built it this way, measured results, and known limits) and the [docs site](https://vibhortayal.github.io/arya/).

## How do I try it? (Demo)

- You can play the same loop as the video: Today, Ask ("We finished the Greek yogurt"), Start shopping, and Lists under More. [`README.md`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md#try-it-in-one-minute)
- These steps need a phone camera or mic: voice add, photo of a note, Find it for me, Map my store, and receipt snap. Everything else works on a laptop.
- Nearly every feature works live in the demo. The staple-judge verdicts were computed beforehand. Only the data (the household, stores and other shoppers) is simulated. Nothing you add is kept after your visit. What the demo household contains: [`assistant/docs/DEMO.md`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/assistant/docs/DEMO.md).
- **Run it yourself** with your own keys (Meta for the AI, Google Places to add stores on your own account): see [Run it yourself](/docs/run-it-yourself). It has a prompt that lets [an AI agent set it up for you](/docs/run-it-yourself#let-your-ai-agent-set-it-up). The [setup in the README](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md#run-it-yourself) also works.
- **Want an account?** Sign-up is invite only while I harden the cost guard rails. Tap "Join the waitlist" on the [landing page](https://arya.teamnightshift.org) and contact me ([support@teamnightshift.org](mailto:support@teamnightshift.org) or [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/vibhortayal)); judges can be approved.

## Does it matter to real people? (Impact)

**What is the real-world potential?** Everyone who shops for a household does the same weekly work. They keep the list in their heads, try not to rebuy what is already in the cupboard, and wonder where the money went. A receipt has all of that, and nobody reads it. Arya reads it, checks every line against the printed total, and turns it into a list with reasons ([how it works](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md#what-is-arya)). On my own 114 receipts (1,226 lines), every one passed the arithmetic check. About 4 in 5 of the staple judge's suggestions matched my own purchase rhythm (precision 0.79 against a purchase-cadence proxy; [measured results](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md#measured-results)).

**Who benefits, and how much does it matter?** People who feed a household or a group, and share a list ([who it is for](/docs/principles)). Shopping is a weekly chore and a household cost, not a rare event. I have not measured time or money saved. I tested on one household, so I do not claim a number ([Known limits](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md#what-are-the-known-limits)).

**Could it become something people use?** It already runs: it is live, installable and free. It has a demo that needs no account, shared lists for groups, a Lists API, and an MCP connector so an agent can edit your lists ([agent connector](/docs/guide/agent-connector)). Store maps already merge across shoppers, so each trip helps the next. Shared prices are planned and not switched on. It runs as one server today. The plan to scale it is in the [roadmap](/docs/roadmap). I built the base. The more people use Arya, the better it gets for them.

**Why this is built for our world:** it is a shopping problem I had myself ([why Arya exists](/docs/principles)), and it is free to use. What existed before Oct 27, and a dated table of what I made in the window, are in [`docs/WHAT-WE-BUILT.md`](/docs/what-we-built).

## Which Meta models does it use, and for what? (Meta AI tooling)

Arya uses six Meta products plus the Meta Model API. Each has one job. Every call goes through one module, [`assistant/api/meta_client.py`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/assistant/api/meta_client.py). The full table, with where each one is in the code, is in [`docs/quest/META-PRODUCTS.md`](/docs/quest/meta-products).

- Spark reads receipt photos first. Wonder re-reads a receipt only if the arithmetic checks flag it. Code: [`decode/service.py`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/assistant/api/decode/service.py), [`checks.py`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/assistant/api/decode/checks.py).
- Muse Spark Open (open weights, hosted on Baseten) is the second seat on the staple judge. It sees item names only. [`open_client.py`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/assistant/api/open_client.py)
- SAM 3.1 draws boxes around shelf items. It pixelates the people it detects before any frame is kept. If that step fails, the frame is thrown away. Detection is not perfect, and I have not scored it. [`shelfscan.py`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/assistant/api/shelfscan.py)
- Muse can use Arya. Any assistant that supports MCP can connect to Arya's MCP address. Muse is the reference client. I tested it end to end on my own Muse on 2026-11-02. It read my list, added items and filed receipts through six tools. Setup and details: [README, "Muse can use Arya"](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md#why-i-built-it-this-way), [agent connector](/docs/guide/agent-connector), code in [`mcp.py`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/assistant/api/mcp.py).
- Available but not used: Muse Glimmer (open weights, self-hosted) and the Spark Contributor tier (cheaper, with different data terms). The reasons are in [`docs/MODELS.md`](/docs/architecture/models).
- Built with Muse Code. It wrote the first version of the engine. The Meta Muse agent on my VM (Muse Spark, which used Muse Wonder) coded in parallel with Claude. The 253 commits named "Spark" are its work. Details: [README, "How this was built"](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md#how-this-was-built).

### Which model does which job?

| Meta product | Id | Job | Measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Muse Spark 1.3 (Standard) | `muse-spark-1.3` | Reads receipt photos first; staple judge, Curator, Ask Arya, list and date photos, shelf labels, crop checks | 92 of 98 lines on the Wonder comparison set; staple precision 0.79. [Details](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md#measured-results) |
| Muse Wonder 1.0 | `muse-wonder-1.0` | Re-reads a receipt the checks flag, or when Spark fails | 97 of 98 lines after hand adjudication, read alone. [Details](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md#measured-results) |
| SAM 3.1 | via Meta Model API | Finds shelves and signs, boxes items for Find it for me, pixelates the people it detects | Used in the guided store scan |
| Muse Voice Transcribe | `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0` | Dictation for the list mic and Ask Arya | n/a |
| Muse Image 1.0 | `muse-image-1.0` | The 23 grab-celebration characters (generated once) and share looks (live, per tap) | n/a |
| Muse Spark Open | `meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026` (hosted on Baseten) | Second seat of the staple judge; dictionary labels | 32 of 32 labels agree with hosted Spark; 3 of 4 staple verdicts |

Spark and Wonder run in Meta's Standard mode. The live reader is `auto` (the code default, `ARYA_PHOTO_READER=auto`). Spark reads first, and Wonder re-reads a flagged receipt. I have not yet measured the pair on photos. Every server call goes through one client with a daily spend limit. The history of the reader is in [`assistant/docs/MODEL-POLICY.md`](/docs/architecture/model-policy).

The eval numbers come from one small set (9 public receipts, 98 lines). Scores change from run to run. So quote the gap between the models, not one number alone. The runs, the scorer and the hand adjudication are in [`docs/evals/`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/tree/main/docs/evals/).

## How is it built, and how well? (Technical depth)

- The model proposes and the code checks. Arithmetic reconciliation, returns, cadence and prices are plain code, so a rerun gives the same answer. There is a cost ledger and there are daily spend caps. The full list of claims, and where to check each one, is in the [judge playbook](/docs/quest/judge-playbook#how-is-it-built-technical-depth).
- Why I made these choices (the idea, a PWA, the stack, hosting, the coding model and each Meta model): [README, "Why I built it this way"](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md#why-i-built-it-this-way).
- Tests and decisions: about 1,900 Python tests and 550 web tests (as of Nov 3), and a dated [decision log](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/docs/DECISIONS.md).
- Read more: design decisions, what I could finish in the window and what is pending, and where it stops scaling, in [`docs/TECHNICAL-DEPTH.md`](/docs/architecture/design-decisions).

## What does it not do yet?

- **Data.** I tested on one household's 114 receipts and a public set of 9 receipts. The measured numbers come from small samples.
- **Markets.** I built and tested with US receipts, dollars and stores first. I did not test other markets.
- **Devices.** I tested on one real iPhone. I did not test the Quest-start and live-walk location checks indoors on a real phone. A store with no stored address point cannot be checked.
- **Store maps.** No store comes pre-mapped. A store's map comes only from shoppers' guided scans.
- **Scale.** Arya runs as one server process on one VM. A few dozen people at once is about the limit ([details](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md#what-are-the-known-limits)). Scaling it out is a plan for after judging. It is not built.
- **Demo allowance.** Each demo visit can spend about $2 on live Meta calls. The demo also has a daily cap. When either runs out, the app says so. Lists and everything that needs no live read keep working. **Use a sample receipt** still works.
- **Accounts.** Sign-up is invite only. It is for a few beta testers and hackathon judges ([how to get in](#how-do-i-try-it-demo)). The demo needs no account.
- **Licence.** Arya's own code is MIT licensed ([`LICENSE`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/LICENSE)). The Meta models and third-party code keep their own terms ([`NOTICE.md`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/NOTICE.md)).

# Judge playbook

An eight-minute path through the live demo. Each step says what to do, what you see, and which Meta model is involved. To watch the same path first, with voice and captions, see the [judge walkthrough video](https://youtu.be/cbJflgCXV5U) (3 min 48 s).

**Live demo:** https://arya.teamnightshift.org/ (no account). Use a phone, or a browser window about 390 px wide. Allow the camera and microphone for the steps that use them. The demo household is fictional. Your changes live in a sandbox for your visit only ([what is real, and what is not](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md#what-is-real-and-what-is-not)).

**What you need.**

- For step 6, a grocery receipt photo. Without one, use [the sample receipt photo](/repo/docs/images/sample-receipt.jpg) (a real receipt of mine), tap **Use a sample receipt**, or **Skip**.
- For step 4, if you are not in a store, open [the sample shelf photo](/repo/docs/images/sample-shelf.jpg) (a Trader Joe's soup and broth shelf, a frame from my own video) on a second screen or a computer. Point the phone camera at it. Turn that screen to full brightness and fill the camera view with the image, to avoid glare. Any other shelf photo works too.

---

## The walk, eight minutes

### 1. Front door
Tap **Try it now**. A short sheet ("Hi, I'm Arya") offers **Show me every screen · 2 min** or **Skip for now**. You land on **Today**, with a bar at the top that says the household is a demo. Today shows your next trip, store news from the simulated town (marked Simulated), what is running low (each with a short reason, such as how often you buy it and when you last did), and your lists.

The navigation tab at the bottom is **Today, Spending, Quest, Ask, More**. **More** holds Lists, Receipts, Stores, Help and Settings.

### 2. Lists
Tap **More**, then **Lists**. The demo has a Costcozy list and a Trader Jill's list (the town's stores have fictional names). The Trader Jill's list holds Bananas, Apples, Organic Milk, Tomato Soup and Hummus. You will look for the tomato soup with the shelf camera in step 4. Hummus is the item Demo Town reports out of stock. The other three are on the sample receipt for step 6. Due staples show under **Suggested for** the store where they are usually bought. Tap one to see why. A **Muse Spark 1.3** staple judge decides which items may be suggested (about 4 in 5 of its suggestions matched my own purchase rhythm: precision 0.79 against a purchase-cadence proxy, [details](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md#measured-results)).

### 3. Add items by voice and photo
In a list, use the add row. Type an item, or tap the mic (**Muse Voice Transcribe**) and say "two gallons of milk, eggs, and blueberries". The camera (**Muse Spark** vision) reads a photo of a handwritten note. Adds apply at once, with Undo. On a laptop with no camera, type the items instead. The photo read is shown on a phone.

### 4. Start a quest
To reach Tomato soup, start from the Trader Jill's list: **More**, **Lists**, open it, tap **Start shopping**, then on the Quest tab tap **Start at Trader Jill's**. (On Today, **Start shopping** on the next trip also works, if that trip is Trader Jill's.) The quest opens at that list's store.

- An unmapped store plays as a labelled typical layout ("A guess, not a pin").
- Tap **Got it**: +10 points (the Golden item is worth double). The celebration characters were painted with **Muse Image**. There is no clock and no way to lose.
- When you reach **Tomato soup**, tap **Can't find it**, then **Find it for me**. Aim the camera at the shelf (or at the sample shelf photo). **SAM 3.1** boxes candidates and **Muse Spark** checks each crop. Look for the highlight on a soup carton. If it lands elsewhere, try again closer. From the same place, **The shelf is empty** tells other Arya shoppers it is gone.
- **Map my store** (on the Quest tab) opens the guided scan. Pan along the shelves. SAM 3.1 pixelates the people it detects, and Muse Spark reads sections, aisle signs and prices.

### 5. Ask Arya
Open **Ask**. Type "What am I running low on?", then "We finished the Greek yogurt." The answer comes from the household data. The stated fact becomes an action that the server validates before it applies.

### 6. Finish with a receipt
When the list is done, tap **Head to checkout**, then **Add your receipt**. **Snap the receipt** with a photo, or tap **Use a sample receipt**. Behind the screen, **Muse Spark** reads each line, in Meta's Standard mode, and code checks that the lines add up to the printed total. If Spark fails, or the checks flag the read (the lines do not add up, or too many lines are unsure), **Muse Wonder 1.0** reads the receipt again. The screen names the model only when the checks flag a read: "Read by Muse Spark · checking", then "Checked by Muse Wonder" or "Read by Muse Wonder". A clean Spark read shows no model name. The demo reads the receipt but keeps nothing. Use a sample receipt if you would rather not send one.

**With the sample receipt.** Download [the sample receipt photo](/repo/docs/images/sample-receipt.jpg) (Trader Joe's, Milpitas, Nov 3, 2026; it is my own receipt). It matches the demo's **Trader Jill's** list: bananas, apples and organic milk are on the receipt. Tomato soup is the one you find with the shelf camera, and hummus is the item Demo Town reports out of stock, so neither is on the receipt. On a laptop, pick the file after tapping **Snap the receipt**. On a phone, save it to Photos first. A read takes about 30 seconds, or up to about 90 when Muse Wonder re-reads it. Expect 3 lines (organic milk $4.49, 2 apples $2.38, 2 bananas $0.58) and a total of $7.45 with no tax. Tap **Looks right** to accept the read. The filed receipt, under **More**, **Receipts**, shows **Total checks out**. The sample is built by code, so no model name shows. The card number, auth codes and cashier name are blurred. The receipt is dated before your trip. A real account refuses that. The demo accepts it and says so on screen ("Demo only: this receipt is dated ..., before this trip began"). How the readers score on a public set: [`docs/evals/`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/tree/main/docs/evals/).

---

## What if something fails?

| Symptom | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| "demo rate limit" | Wait a minute and retry. |
| "You've used this demo visit's live reads" | The visit's share (about $2) is spent. Lists, Today, Spending and the rest keep working, and **Use a sample receipt** still works. Only the live reads (receipt, photo, voice, Ask) pause. |
| "The demo's live reads are paused for today" | The demo's shared daily budget is used up. The rest is the same as above. The real app has its own daily budget, so judges cannot use it up. |
| Receipt spinner over 90 s | A receipt that Muse Wonder re-reads can take up to about 90 seconds. Wait, or Skip. |
| Voice gives nothing | Check microphone permission, or type. |
| Page looks stale | Reload twice, or clear site data. |

## What do I do when I am done?

Tap **Finish demo** (top right) to leave feedback, replay the tour or see the code.

---

## Does it matter to real people? (Impact)

The four rubric questions are answered on [the judges page, Impact](/docs/judges#does-it-matter-to-real-people-impact).

## How is it built? (Technical depth)

| Claim | Where to verify |
| --- | --- |
| One module calls the Meta API | [`meta_client.py`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/assistant/api/meta_client.py) |
| Receipts verified by arithmetic | [`test_receipt_math.py`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/assistant/tests/test_receipt_math.py) |
| Demo writes never reach disk | `state.set_overlay` in [`state.py`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/assistant/api/state.py); sandbox tests |
| People are pixelated before a frame is kept | `shelfscan.scrub_people` in [`shelfscan.py`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/assistant/api/shelfscan.py) (fails closed) |
| Model proposes, code checks: arithmetic reconciliation, returns, cadence and prices are deterministic | [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](/docs/architecture/overview) |
| Cheapest model that holds the score, with a ledger, a rate gate and daily spend caps | [`MODEL-POLICY.md`](/docs/architecture/model-policy) |
| Measured results, small samples, stated in Known limits | [`docs/evals/`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/tree/main/docs/evals/), [README, Known limits](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md#what-are-the-known-limits) |
| Open API and docs | https://arya.teamnightshift.org/developers |
| Outside services: the Google Places API finds stores for the store picker; Supabase, Resend and Baseten | [README, Built with](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md#built-with) |
| Tests | `cd assistant && python -m unittest discover -s tests`; known failures in [`STATUS.md`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/STATUS.md). CI is manual-only (`.github/workflows/tests.yml`) |
| How the build was run (roles, hard rules, review and test gates) | [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/AGENTS.md) |
| Build diary, one log per work session | [`assistant/loops/`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/tree/main/assistant/loops/); how the early commits arrived fast: [README, "How this was built"](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md#how-this-was-built) |

Read more: design decisions, what I could finish in the window and what is pending, and where it stops scaling, in [`docs/TECHNICAL-DEPTH.md`](/docs/architecture/design-decisions).

## What is not in the demo?

- Imports and batch jobs are switched off in the demo (bulk receipt imports, PDF and text decode, the Curator and staple-judge batch runs).
- Friends, the Store and Global boards, and Shop-Off and Spotter reports show only your own account's data (plus labelled samples), in the real app too. Shelf-empty reports are shared between shoppers in the real app (three shoppers must report the same item at a store, and only shoppers with that item on their list see it). A demo report reaches no one, because the demo writes to its own sandbox.
- Open weights are used in one place: Muse Spark Open (hosted on Baseten) is the second seat of the staple judge. It sees item names only, never personal data. Glimmer is not used.

Everything else it does not do yet, for the real app too: [the judges page, "What does it not do yet?"](/docs/judges#what-does-it-not-do-yet).

<!-- https://docs.arya.teamnightshift.org/docs/intro -->

# What is Arya

Arya is a grocery app that learns how you shop from your receipts and helps shoppers help each other. It puts the whole grocery chore in one place: shared lists, a guided route through the store, a clear view of your spend and usage, and out-of-stock warnings from other shoppers.

**Groceries are an integral part of our lives.** Hunters and gatherers did it to survive. Think about what it takes today.

You have many lists in your notes. Your partner adds items over text while they are shopping at a different store. So **both of you bought yogurt, and neither bought the toilet paper that ran out.** Oh, and **the store shelf for the milk your kids need is empty.** The receipts end up in the trash, so **you never see how the money was spent,** or that the same item was cheaper at another store. **That cheese you bought a few weeks ago went bad** before anyone used it.

> *You hold all of it in your head, and it's still never quite right.*

I built Arya for this hackathon to manage groceries in one place: shared lists, guided store routes, spend and usage insights, and community powered alerts. The idea is simple. When shoppers share what they learn, where items are located, what's cheaper, what's out of stock, every trip gets a little easier.

---

**Arya is not just a chatbot on a grocery list.** Using Muse Wonder, I created Arya's learning engine to understand my household usage from my Costco receipts. Arya showed me patterns in my shopping. Arya also drafts my next list based on what we use.

**I add items** by typing, speaking, or taking a photo of a handwritten list. And Arya makes the chore more fun with **Quest mode**, which turns shopping into a game.

**Before heading out for my quest,** Arya warns me if an item from my list is out of stock. **In the store,** it guides me aisle by aisle. If I need help spotting an item, I point the camera at a shelf: **SAM** finds the item, **Spark** points me to it, and I move forward with my quest. If an item is out of stock, I tap **Not here**, and the next shopper knows.

**At checkout** I snap the receipt. **Spark** reads it, and if needed, **Muse Wonder** takes a second look. And the learning engine improves with every trip.

**Back home,** Arya tells me if something from my previous trips is about to go bad. And when I use up an item, I just tell Arya we're out, and it's on the list automagically.

---

**Arya is soft launched.** The demo is open to everyone, but accounts are invite-only for beta testers. I also integrated the **Meta Muse** AI agent over **MCP** to talk to Arya. A [developer portal](https://arya.teamnightshift.org/developers) is live for API integrations.

During the hackathon, I built the first step. Arya gets wiser with every shared list, every receipt, every "Not here" tap.

> **Humans helping humans.**
>
> **This is Arya.**

*Built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026 (Team Nightshift, Indie track).*

# Built in the hackathon window

The hackathon window opened on Oct 27, 2026. This page says what existed
before it, what I made in it and when, taken from git. Times are US Eastern.
What git cannot show is listed under "What git cannot confirm".

## What existed before the window

- **The idea search.** By my own account it took about two days. The commits for
  it are in a separate research repo ([`vibhortayal/meta-hackathon-research`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/meta-hackathon-research)). They start
  on Oct 26 at 12:37. The 28 commits that day, up to 16:51, hold candidate ideas
  and a plan for spikes, with no spike results. This is before Oct 27, and I
  say so plainly.
- **My 114 Costco receipts** (back to 2023) are my own purchase history, imported
  as data. They are not in this repo.
- **The server.** The Oracle VM already existed for my other hobby projects.
  Setting up Arya on it began on Oct 27.
- **Nothing in the Arya repo is older than Oct 27, 15:13 ET.** Its first commit
  already holds the design documents (`SPEC.md` and `IMPLEMENTATION.md`, about
  900 lines), which I wrote before committing them.

## What I made, and when

| When (ET) | What | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Oct 27, morning | Grocery Navigator brainstorm notes, stamped 11:37 and 11:46 | research repo, `IDEAS-owner-brainstorm.md` |
| Oct 27, 13:50 | Spike 1: receipt decode on 7 real Costco PDFs with Muse Spark, arithmetic matched 7 of 7, $0.20 | research repo, `89ff3ab` |
| Oct 27, 14:26 | Spike 2: photo receipts with Spark, 32 of 32 lines on 4 receipts (5 photos) | research repo, `218f332`, `6ca6d7f` |
| Oct 27, 14:29 | Spike B: the Costco pull test hit a bot wall, so I chose receipt uploads | research repo, `a2ef346` |
| Oct 27, 15:03 to 15:06 | My Costco receipts staged: 63, then 114 | research repo, `25cba97`, `f1cbdd0` |
| Oct 27, 15:13 | **First Arya commit** | `ca9d3ee` |
| Oct 27, 15:31 to 15:38 | Decode, item dictionary, ledger and patterns, and the first phone app land in four commits | `e134814` to `b210863` |
| Oct 27, 15:43 to 15:52 | Public HTTPS, then the DuckDNS address | `e326e348`, `c2430d6d` |
| Oct 27, 16:02 to 16:03 | Photo decode path and Gate 0 verdict, PASS (9 public photos, hand labels) | `cb907e3d`, `e7ebb235`; research repo `39d6433` |
| Oct 27, 21:00 | Muse Wonder commissioned to author the store-frame localizer | `881b115` |
| Oct 27, 21:12 | Model policy amendment: Wonder reads photos through Nov 4 (superseded Nov 2: Spark first, Wonder on flagged receipts, through Nov 9) | `c01c007a` |
| Oct 27, 22:19 | Wonder's first localizer spike vendored as `api/localizer.py` (removed Oct 29, `51cab53`) | `47b2471` |
| Oct 27, 22:59 | Photo decode switched to Wonder | `7f32f2f` |
| Oct 27, 23:02 | Wonder-vs-Spark eval committed in the research repo | `b39a961` |
| Oct 28 | Accounts, the judge front door; Supabase, Resend and Baseten set up | |
| Oct 30 | teamnightshift.org registered at Cloudflare; live site moved to arya.teamnightshift.org with invite-only sign-in | |
| Oct 31 to Nov 2 | Hardening, the navigation tab, lists, the Kroger aisle lookup, docs, "Run it yourself" | |

The Wonder eval is the one the model policy cites. On the 9 Gate 0 photos (98
hand-labeled lines), Wonder scored 97/98 and Spark 92/98. The Wonder figure is after hand adjudication; Spark's is from the automatic scorer, which gives Wonder 86 of 98. Price errors were 0 for Wonder and
4 for Spark, for $4.47 of model spend. Why Spark shows 92 here and 90 at Gate 0 is
explained once, under the model map in [For judges](/docs/judges#which-model-does-which-job).

## What git cannot confirm

- **Who wrote the first engine commits.** Muse Code, running Muse Wonder, wrote
  the first version of the engine with me. Git lists those commits under the author name "Spark", at 15:31 to
  15:38 on Oct 27. Git records no model or tool, so the author name alone does
  not show it. That is my account of it.
- **The other "Spark" commits.** 253 of the 1,333 commits are named "Spark".
  They come from the Meta Muse agent on my VM. It ran Muse Spark and used
  Muse Wonder through the agent, and it coded in parallel with Claude. Git records the
  author name only, so the name alone does not show it. That is my account of it.
- **When the Muse Wonder spike sessions ran.** No start or end time is recorded
  for them, and the spike folders the docs mention are in neither repo. I give
  no date for them.

## What exists today

The 3-minute video cannot show everything. This list is the standout parts
of Arya that exist today, each with why it matters and where the detail lives.
Everything here is built and in the code. Ideas that are not built are on the
[After the hackathon](/docs/roadmap) page. For the product in full, see
[`assistant/docs/SPEC.md`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/assistant/docs/SPEC.md) and
[`assistant/docs/USER-JOURNEYS.md`](/docs/guide/user-journeys).

## Receipts you can trust
- **A model reads, code checks.** Muse Spark reads a receipt photo first (Wonder is the backup
  reader). Plain code then checks every line
  against the printed total before anything posts. *Why:* a wrong price never
  goes in silently. [`assistant/docs/MODEL-POLICY.md`](/docs/architecture/model-policy), [`docs/evals/`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/tree/main/docs/evals/)
- **Returns net out** against purchases.
- **"To check"** marks lines Arya is unsure about. **Fix this line** edits the
  name, quantity and price, with Undo. The printed total never changes.
  The original photo is kept. *Why:* you stay in control of your record.
- **Background reading with progress:** several receipts at once, and you can
  leave while Arya reads them.

## A list that learns
- **Patterns from your own receipts:** how often you buy each item and what you
  pay at each store. From that, the list shows what is **running low** and what to
  **use soon**, each with a reason (the "why" sheet).
- **A staple judge with two seats:** Muse Spark decides what counts as a staple.
  Muse Spark Open (open weights, hosted on Baseten) judges again from item names
  only. Disagreements are kept for review. *Why:* names advise, purchase facts
  decide. [`assistant/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](/docs/architecture/overview)
- **The Curator** proposes product merges and splits with reasons; nothing
  changes until you apply it.
- **Your own lists, and every item sits on one:** you make your own lists, for example, one for each store, such as Trader Jill's or Costcozy. When you add an item, it goes to the list you say,
  or to your only list, or Arya asks "Which list?".
- **Works offline (signed-in accounts):** lists and other screens show as last saved, and list edits
  queue until you are back online. Receipts, Ask, photos, voice and sharing need a connection. Signed-in accounts keep a cached copy. The demo saves offline list changes for that visit only.

## Prices from your own receipts
- Cheaper store, price trend, similar items per ounce, which store to buy each
  item at, and the cost of food waste, on a Spending screen. *Why:* nothing
  is fetched from store sites, flyers or the web, so every figure is yours.
  [`assistant/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](/docs/architecture/overview)
- Community prices and live "how busy is the store" are not live; the opt-in
  records a choice only (`SPEC.md`, FR-11.7).

## Ask Arya
- A chat over a snapshot of your household's data that can also act on
  statements such as "we finished the yogurt".
- Answers in the language you write; Spanish and Hindi were the ones verified
  ([`assistant/docs/MULTILINGUAL-ASK.md`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/assistant/docs/MULTILINGUAL-ASK.md)).
- Voice dictation and a photo of a handwritten list.

## Quest, the optional game
- A hunt through a model of your store with **no clock and no way to lose**.
  Start shopping on a list opens it at that list's store and ends on your
  receipt. [`docs/quest/GAME-DESIGN.md`](/docs/quest/game-design)
- **Find it for me:** point the camera at a shelf; SAM 3.1 boxes candidates and
  Muse Spark checks each one.
- **Map my store:** a guided camera scan. SAM 3.1 pixelates the people it
  detects before anything is kept. If that fails, the frame is discarded. Detection is not perfect and is not scored. A store counts as mapped only where it has a usable,
  fresh photo, so the status is earned. [`docs/quest/MAP-MY-STORE.md`](/docs/quest/map-my-store)
- **Build a store** from three questions, practice in it, and save it.

## Groups and everyday use
- **Groups** share lists between the people you live with, joined by a
  single-use code or an invite link. Receipts stay with whoever filed them.
- **Daily reminders** for what is running low. Live on the hosted app. You opt in, and on iPhone the app must be added to the Home Screen first.
- **Add to Home Screen**, so it opens like an app.
- A navigation tab (the bottom buttons) you arrange yourself.

## Transparency about AI and cost
- **Keeping Arya running** (Settings, About Arya) shows your own AI use by kind
  (receipts and photos, Ask, store maps, lists and voice), this month and since
  you joined, and the whole app's AI cost and who pays. *Why:* Arya is free, and
  the paid AI reading is shown openly.
- **How Arya uses AI** says where AI is used and when to double-check, and that
  Arya is not a food-safety check.
- **Arya's powers** lists what Arya does for you now and what turns on as you
  add receipts.
- **Guards:** a daily budget for the real app and a separate one for the demo,
  a per-visit cap on the demo, and a heads-up and pause for unusually heavy use.
  [`assistant/docs/OPS.md`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/assistant/docs/OPS.md)

## Open, and bring your own tools
- **Lists API and developer portal** at `/developers` (quickstart in curl, Python
  and JavaScript, interactive reference). [`docs/API.md`](/docs/api/lists-api)
- **A connector for your own AI agent (MCP):** Make my code, then ask the Muse
  agent to connect. [`assistant/docs/AGENT-CONNECTOR.md`](/docs/guide/agent-connector)

## Built to run
- One image, also run locally with Docker in a few steps
  ([`docs/RUN-IT-YOURSELF.md`](/docs/run-it-yourself)).
- A `/health` check that shows the running commit, nightly backups, and an
  owner-only Ops screen with a daily report, a pause switch for paid reads,
  spend ceilings and a cost ledger with one row per model call.
- Tests and measured results: [`STATUS.md`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/STATUS.md), [`docs/evals/`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/tree/main/docs/evals/).

## In the code but switched off
- **Use your own Meta key (unfinished, not used).** A Settings row, a Help topic,
  an Ask answer and a sign-up door. An account with its own key would never fall
  back to Arya's keys. I decided not to use it, so it is switched off
  and not part of the demo.
  [After the hackathon](/docs/roadmap)
- **Alexa skill (built, switched off, not tested on a real device).** An Alexa
  skill that adds items to your Arya list by voice. The code is merged (#515,
  #516) behind the `ARYA_ALEXA` flag, which is off. I paused it until after the
  hackathon, and it has not been tried on a real Echo. It is voice add only.
  Amazon has retired its Alexa list API, so Arya cannot sync with Alexa's
  own lists.

---

<!-- https://docs.arya.teamnightshift.org/docs/principles -->

# Why Arya exists, and what it stands for

Arya is my answer to "Build for Your World". It puts Meta's models to work in a world I know firsthand: the weekly grocery shop.

## The problem

Keeping track of groceries is a small job that never ends. You remember the list, then forget it at the store. You buy what you already have. You cannot say where the money went. I had this problem, so I built Arya for myself first. How the app solves it, step by step, is in [the README, What is Arya](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md#what-is-arya).

## Who it is for

Shoppers. The people who keep a household or a group fed, and who remember what is running out. If you shop for a household, or share a list with housemates, family or a group, Arya is for you.

## Principles

1. **For shoppers, and built up with them.** The store maps come from shoppers' own scans, and lists are shared by the households and groups who use them. Shoppers helping each other is the point.
2. **Free to use.** It costs money to keep running (the AI reading). You can see what you use in Settings, About Arya, Keeping Arya running. Nothing in it is for sale, there are no ads, and I do not sell your data.
3. **The model proposes, code checks.** A model reads the receipt. Plain code checks every line before anything posts. You can trust the numbers because the arithmetic is checked, not guessed.
4. **Yours by default.** Your receipts and lists are yours. A group sees its members' lists and receipts. If you leave, your receipts go with you. Arya uses no prices from store sites, flyers or the web.
5. **Limits stated.** Built and tested with US receipts, dollars and stores first. Other markets are not tested. What is not live is marked as such. The full list is under [Known limits](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md#what-are-the-known-limits).

## Where to read more

[The README](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md) for the app, [who else is out there](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/docs/quest/BUSINESS.md), [the roadmap](/docs/roadmap) for what is next, and [the decision log](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/docs/DECISIONS.md) for the choices behind it.

---

<!-- https://docs.arya.teamnightshift.org/docs/guide/user-journeys -->

# Arya user journeys

Seven journeys, from the first receipt to a shared household. Each one
has a person, a goal, the screens in order, and sample data. The numbers
come from the demo household (`python -m harness.make_demo_household
data`), so you can open the live demo and see the same thing.

Store names: these journeys use real store names from my own shopping. The hosted demo (Demo Town) uses invented ones, such as Costcozy and Trader Jill's.

The list comes first. The Quest hunt is optional.

## How to read this page

**Status tags**

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Shipped | On `main` and in the demo. |
| Shipped, flag | On `main`, but a setting keeps it off until I turn it on. |
| Needs a model | Works only when `MODEL_API_KEY` is set. The demo uses the key on the VM. |
| Planned | Not built. Listed so nobody thinks it is there. |

**The demo household.** The fictional Sharma family. 39 receipts from
May 2 to Oct 24, 2026: Trader Joe's 18, Costco 12, Safeway 9. Total
spend is $1,115.42. That is $1,090.42 of groceries, plus a $25.00 gift
card (bought for someone else). One chicken was returned for $12.30.
The demo slides all dates to the current week. The screenshots were
taken on Oct 29, 2026, so a date such as "Oct 19" in a picture is a
seed date moved forward. Money amounts never move.

**Where prices come from.** Every price in this page comes from the
household's own receipts. Arya does not scrape stores, read flyers or search the web for
prices, and it calls no store API for prices. (Google Places finds stores for the
store picker, and Kroger's API gives aisle hints; neither supplies prices.)

**Screenshots** are real 390x844 captures of the demo, in
`assistant/docs/img/`.

---

## Journey 1. First receipt, and the list starts to write itself

**Person.** Priya Sharma. She shops every Saturday. She writes lists in
her head and forgets milk.

**Goal.** Put in last week's receipts and see what Arya learns.

**Status.** Shipped. Reading the photo or PDF needs a model.

| Step | What Priya does | What Arya shows |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Opens the app, taps **Try it now** or creates an account. | Landing: "Your grocery run, smarter." Three real rows (Whole Milk "Running low"). |
| 2 | Lists, **Receipts** (the group at the bottom), **Add receipts**. She picks the Costco PDF from Oct 17. More than one file is fine. | One progress line per file, then one summary: filed, already filed, could not read. |
| 3 | Waits a few seconds. | Muse Spark reads the lines. Code adds them up. The receipt shows a check mark and its total only if the lines match the printed total. |
| 4 | Files the same PDF again by mistake. | "Already filed." Arya compares a fingerprint (store, date, lines, total) and does not count the trip twice. |
| 5 | Wants one old receipt. In **Receipts**, types the store in the search box, opens **Date** and picks a range, and picks **Store A to Z** or **Highest total** in **Sort**. | A line shows how many receipts match and their total. **Clear** removes the filters. |
| 6 | Spots a misread line on a filed receipt. Opens it, taps the line, and changes the name, quantity or price in **Fix this line**. | The line shows an "edited" tag. A new name also fixes the item on her other receipts. The printed total never changes. If the lines stop adding up, the receipt says so and no longer counts as checked. **Undo** puts the old values back. In a group, any member can fix a line, but only the person who filed the receipt can delete it. |
| 7 | Opens **Today**. | **Running low** lists items that are due. |

**Sample data: the Costco receipt, Oct 17**

| Line | Price |
|---|---|
| Pasture Eggs 12 ct | $6.47 |
| Jasmine Rice 10 lb | $13.49 |
| Paper Towels 6 ct | $9.99 |
| AA Batteries 8 ct | $8.99 |
| Kirkland Organic Milk 0.5 gal | $4.14 |
| **Total** | **$43.08** (the lines add up, so it posts) |

**What she learns on Today.** After 26 Saturdays the pattern for Whole
Milk is clear: "Every ~7 days; last bought 10 days ago", window Oct 24
to Oct 27. Sourdough Loaf has the same line. Each row has an **Add**
button.

![Today](/repo/assistant/docs/img/j-today.png)

**The rules behind it**
- A pattern needs 3 kept buys before Arya calls an item "running low".
- Returns count as not bought. The returned chicken (Oct 5, $12.30)
  never comes back as a suggestion.
- Bad lines go to a review queue. Nothing posts in silence.
- The gift card is tracked under "Bought for others". It is never
  suggested.

![Receipts](/repo/assistant/docs/img/j-receipts.png)

---

## Journey 2. Plan a Costco and Trader Joe's trip

**Person.** Priya, on Friday evening.

**Goal.** One list per store, with the usual things already there.

**Status.** Shipped. Typing and tapping are code. Voice and photo adds
need a model.

_Update 2026-11-02: "Everything else" is no longer an automatic list (it exists only if you make one), and Lists now sits under More. The steps below and their screenshot show the earlier layout and are due a re-walk._

| Step | What Priya does | What Arya shows |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Taps **Lists**. | Cards: **Costco** (2 items), **Trader Joe's** (3 items), **Everything else** (1 item). |
| 2 | Opens **Trader Joe's**. | Avocados 4 ct, Pasta 1 lb x2, Hummus. Under them, suggestions from her patterns for this store. |
| 3 | Types "mlik" in the add row and taps **Add**. | The add applies at once, with Undo. Arya links the typed name to the tracked item, so "mlik" becomes Whole Milk 1 gal. |
| 4 | Taps Whole Milk to see why. | The **why sheet** (below). |
| 5 | Swipes Basil to **Move**. | Basil goes to the Trader Joe's list. She can use **Select** to move many items. |
| 6 | Taps the pencil by the list name. | The name edits in place. |

**Sample data: lists after the setup**

| List | Items |
|---|---|
| Costco (store: Costco) | Paper Towels 6 ct, Jasmine Rice 10 lb |
| Trader Joe's (store: Trader Joe's) | Avocados 4 ct, Pasta 1 lb (x2), Hummus |
| Everything else | Basil |

![Lists](/repo/assistant/docs/img/j-lists.png)

**The why sheet for Whole Milk** shows Arya's reasons in plain words:
"You buy it every ~7 days. 25 times since May." "Last bought 10 days
ago. That is 3 days past your usual." Price lines follow in Journey 4.

![Why sheet](/repo/assistant/docs/img/j-why.png)

**Also on this screen**
- Typing "milk" finds "Whole Milk". Typing a non-grocery item, for
  example "light bulbs", keeps it under Other errands.
- Items you add are not changed without your tap. Riskier changes
  (out of stock, never again, snooze) ask first.
- Planned: none for this journey.

---

## Journey 3. In the store with Quest

**Person.** Priya, Saturday at Trader Joe's.

**Goal.** Get everything on the list without walking back.

**Status.** Shipped. A quest needs no model. "Find it for me" needs one.
Express, the plain-checklist mode, no longer has an entry point. Its
screen stays only for runs started before it was removed.

| Step | What Priya does | What Arya shows |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Opens the Trader Joe's list. Taps **Start shopping · 3 items**. | A first-time how-to: Find it, Grab it, Snap the receipt. A list with no items sends her to Add items instead. |
| 2 | Taps **Got it**. | "Trader Joe's · Quest", a points counter, "0 of 3". The store's layout is labelled as a typical layout until shoppers map it. A card says "Pasta 1 lb x2, Pasta Shelf". |
| 3 | Taps **Grab**. | +10 points. She can put an item back. |
| 4 | An item is not on the shelf. She taps **Not here?** and confirms. | The report is shared. Once three different shoppers have reported the same item at a store, other shoppers who have it on their list and use that store see a "3 shoppers say not here" alert on Today. |
| 5 | Taps **Find it for me** and aims the camera at a shelf. | SAM 3.1 boxes candidates, Muse Spark checks each one, and the match lights up for one tap. |
| 6 | Taps **I'm done shopping**, then photographs the receipt. | +50 points. The receipt is filed with the same checks as Journey 1. |

**Rules.** No clock. No lives. No way to lose. Quest is optional. The
list works without it.

**Sample data.** "Trader Joe's · Quest", 3 items on the card: Avocados 4
ct, Pasta 1 lb x2, Hummus.

---

## Journey 4. Compare prices from my own receipts

**Person.** Arjun Sharma, who pays the bills and wants to spend less.

**Goal.** Find out where milk is cheaper, and what has gone up.

**Status.** Shipped. Arya uses only the household's own receipts.
Community prices, **Deals** and **Arya Shoppers** are Planned. Today the
opt-in choice is saved and nothing else is built. There are no price
charts. Trends show as words and percent.

| Step | What Arya shows | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | "Whole Milk 1 gal: $4.17 at Safeway. You usually pay $4.56 at Trader Joe's." | Today, **Store alerts** |
| 2 | "Up 10% since May. $4.31 then, $4.76 now, at Trader Joe's." | Whole Milk why sheet |
| 3 | "Cheaper at Safeway: $4.40. You paid $4.76 at Trader Joe's. Safeway on Oct 19." | Whole Milk why sheet |
| 4 | "Similar items you bought. This one: 3.4 cents/oz. Kirkland Organic Milk 0.5 gal, $4.14, Costco, 6.5 cents/oz." | Whole Milk why sheet |
| 5 | The **(i)** button on each line gives the small print, for example how many buys the number comes from. | Why sheet |

**Sample data: milk price by store (own receipts)**

| Store | Buys | Median | Last |
|---|---|---|---|
| Trader Joe's | 16 | $4.54 | $4.76 |
| Safeway | 9 | $4.17 | $4.40 |

Eggs are different. Arya has 12 Costco buys (median $6.03, last $6.47,
up 17% since May) and one Trader Joe's buy at $6.96. It shows no "cheaper
at" line, because there is no better store in the data.

![Why sheet with price lines](/repo/assistant/docs/img/j-why.png)

**Spending, "Your prices over time"** (the Spending page, called Analysis before the labels audit)

| Card | What it says |
|---|---|
| Your basket | "Your basket costs 1.5% more than in June. Same 14 items you buy often. About $4.04 more a month." Movers: Sourdough Loaf +6.6%, Pasture Eggs +5.9%, Greek Yogurt +5.3%. |
| Split smarter | "Save about $2.61 a month. Buy Whole Milk 1 gal and Bananas at Safeway." Milk $1.48, bananas $1.13. |
| Spend | Oct 2026 total $165.39. By store (all time, not just October): Trader Joe's $453.55, Safeway $396.21, Costco $265.66. Top item: Chicken Breast, $152.21. |

![Analysis](/repo/assistant/docs/img/j-analysis.png)

**Arya's powers.** Settings, About Arya, has a page that lists what Arya already
does and what turns on next, with one line per power. One "Did you
know?" line shows on Today each day.

![Powers](/repo/assistant/docs/img/j-powers.png)

**Limits.** Arya says "your prices" and never "the store's price". With
no receipt for an item at a store, it makes no claim for that store.
Spark never finds or guesses a price.

---

## Journey 5. A household with Groups

**People.** Priya and her partner Arjun. Each has their own account on
their own phone.

**Goal.** One shared set of lists and receipts. A clean way out.

**Status.** Shipped, on by default in `docker-compose.yml`
(`ARYA_GROUPS=1`, PR #128). Set `ARYA_GROUPS=0` in `deploy/.env` to turn
it off. The demo household cannot join a group, so this journey needs
two real accounts. It needs a deploy before the live site has it.
Live sync uses Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY when `DATABASE_URL` is set.
It has not been tried against the Supabase session pooler. If the
pooler refuses it, set `ARYA_LIVE_PG=0`.

| Step | Who | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Priya | Settings, **Start a group**, names it "Sharma home". Her lists become the group's lists. She is the owner. |
| 2 | Priya | Taps **Invite someone**. Arya shows a 6-character code, for example `K7M2QX`. It lasts 48 hours. Any member can make one. A group holds up to 6 people. |
| 3 | Arjun | Opens **Join a group**, types the code. Arya shows a preview first: who invited, how many people, how many lists. |
| 4 | Arjun | Joins. His lists merge into the group's. Lists with the same name become one list. Both people now see Costco and Trader Joe's. |
| 5 | Arjun | Adds Hummus to Trader Joe's in the aisle. |
| 6 | Priya | Her open list reloads in about a second. A tab skips the echo of its own change. |
| 7 | Both | Receipts from both accounts show in **Receipts**, tagged with the person who filed each one. |

**Leaving**

| Step | What happens |
|---|---|
| 1 | Arjun taps **Leave group**. The sheet says: "You keep a copy of the lists and your own receipts." |
| 2 | He taps **Leave group** again. |

| Data | After he leaves |
|---|---|
| Lists | Duplicated. Arjun has a copy. The group keeps its own. |
| Receipts | Belong to the account that filed them. Each goes with its owner. |
| Running low, patterns, spend | Recomputed for both sides from the receipts each side now has. |
| Personal items (profile, badges, Quest, push, currency) | Never shared, so nothing changes. |

If the owner leaves, the member who joined first becomes owner. When the
last member leaves, the group is gone.

**Not planned.** Roles, per-list privacy, kids' accounts.

---

## Journey 6. Expiry dates and Use soon

**Person.** Priya, unpacking the Saturday shop.

**Goal.** Use the spinach before it turns.

**Status.** Shipped. Reading a date from a photo needs a model. In the
demo, a canned sample read stands in for the photo.

| Step | What Priya does | What Arya shows |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Taps **+ Snap a date** on Today, then photographs "USE BY OCT 31" on the spinach. | Spark reads the date. Arya shows what it read: "Baby Spinach 16 oz, use by Oct 31". |
| 2 | Taps **Looks right, track it**. | Nothing is saved until she confirms. The photo is never kept. |
| 3 | Looks at Today three days later. | **Use soon** shows Baby Spinach 16 oz with the days left. It shows items up to 7 days ahead. A past date stays for 7 days, then fades. |
| 4 | Taps the row in Use soon. | She can snooze it (it waits 2 days), fix the date or stop tracking. |
| 5 | Buys spinach again. | A new receipt means a new package, so the old date drops. |

**Still good?** Arya asks by itself when an item "usually turns about
now". The demo shows **Still good? · 3 to check**: Baby Spinach 16 oz,
Chicken Breast and 1 more. Priya taps **Still good** or **It expired**.
This part is code, not a model.

**Rule for a past date.** A past date is neutral ("your call"), not a
red alarm.

---

## Journey 7. Ask in the aisle, a reminder, and the Home Screen

**Person.** Priya, in the week.

**Goal.** Get answers without opening a spreadsheet, and get a nudge
before milk runs out.

### 7a. Ask Arya

**Status.** Shipped. **Needs a model.** Without `MODEL_API_KEY` the
Ask tab says it could not answer.

In the Ask tab Priya can type, or tap **Talk** to speak. Arya answers in text only:

| She says | Arya does |
|---|---|
| "We finished the Greek yogurt." | Applies the change and the list updates. |
| "What do we spend on coffee?" | Answers from the ledger (Coffee Beans 12 oz, $104.80 over 26 weeks in the demo). It does not invent a number. |
| "Where is milk cheaper?" | Reads the price facts that code computed from her receipts (see Journey 4). The model only reads them. |
| "What is Arya?" | Answers about Arya itself. |
| A photo (Photo chip under the Ask field) | Opens a chooser over the existing readers (list, receipt, fridge, expiry date), or "Ask about this photo" once. The photo is not stored. |

**During a hunt** a bar "Ask Arya..." sits at the bottom. It opens a
sheet with three quick questions: "Where's the {item}?", "Is there a
cheaper one?", "I can't find it". The sheet knows the store, the item
on screen and what is left, so "this" and "it" work.

### 7b. Push reminder

**Status.** Shipped, live on the hosted app (flag `ARYA_PUSH_REMINDERS=1`,
VAPID keys, daily cron at 13:00 UTC; enabled Nov 2). Setup is in
`assistant/docs/PUSH-REMINDERS.md`. Demo accounts never see it.

1. Settings, Preferences, **Remind me**. Priya turns it on and picks the notice
   window (1 to 7 days, default 2).
2. At 9:00 the daily job runs. It sends at most one push per account
   per day. No model call. $0.
3. Example push, one item: **"Whole Milk 1 gal is probably running
   out"** with "Add it to this week's list? Tap to open your list."
4. Example push, several: **"3 things are about to run out"** with
   "Whole Milk 1 gal, Sourdough Loaf, Pasture Eggs 12 ct. Tap to see
   them."
5. A cycle is announced once. A new receipt starts a new cycle.

On iPhone, reminders work only after Add to Home Screen (iOS 16.4 or
newer).

### 7c. Add Arya to the Home Screen

**Status.** Shipped (PR #133). Hidden in the demo and once Arya runs
from the Home Screen.

| Phone | What happens |
|---|---|
| Android and desktop Chrome | A card at the top of Today: **Add Arya to your Home Screen. Full screen, with reminders.** The **Install** button runs the browser's own prompt. |
| iPhone | The card says **Show how**. It opens 4 steps, including "leave Open as Web App on". Off means a plain Safari tab, and then push cannot work. |

The card shows from the second visit, only when the list has an item.
If Priya taps the cross, it stays away for 30 days. Settings always has
an **Add to Home Screen** row while installing is possible.

<!-- https://docs.arya.teamnightshift.org/docs/quest/overview -->

# Arya Quest: doc pack

Quest is the optional game layer of Arya, a grocery app that learns how you
shop from your receipts and helps shoppers help each other (see the root `README.md`). Team Nightshift,
Indie track, submission Nov 4, 2026, 9:00 PM ET.

Quest turns your grocery list into a treasure hunt in your real store. Pick the store. Arya sorts your list by where you usually buy
each thing. Walk the hunt through real photos of the aisles and grab each
item (points only go up, no clock). With **Find it for me**, you point
the camera at the shelf and the item lights up. Snap the receipt at checkout. It banks your
points and teaches Arya your household, so next week's list writes
itself.

An unmapped store still plays, as a labelled typical layout. A guided
camera scan maps it for every shopper after you.

## Loop

**Plan → Find → Grab → Receipt.**

1. **Plan.** The list arrives in any form (photo, paste, typing, voice,
   Muse chat). Pick the store. The list is sorted for it from your
   receipts.
2. **Find.** Shoppers' photos where a store section is mapped (people
   pixelated by SAM 3.1), and a labelled typical layout elsewhere. Find it for me: SAM 3.1 boxes candidates,
   and Muse Spark verifies them.
3. **Grab.** +10 per grab, milestones, a full-haul bonus. Shortage
   reports and sightings feed a live store map.
4. **Receipt.** Muse Spark reads it (Spark first; see the model map in
   `JUDGES.md`). Code checks the arithmetic. The receipt then
   feeds patterns, spend and returns.

## Documents

| File | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| [GAME-DESIGN.md](/docs/quest/game-design) | Rules, loop, rewards, Spotter, community |
| [UX.md](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/docs/archive/quest/UX.md) | Sessions, flow, store view, intake. Oct 27 rules, archived on 2026-11-04; the wireframes are the design of record |
| [wireframes.html](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/docs/quest/wireframes.html) | Clickable design of record |
| [game-flow-prototype.html](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/docs/quest/game-flow-prototype.html) | The game flow, tap through on one phone |
| [ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/docs/quest/ARCHITECTURE.md) | Data planes and pipelines |
| [META-PRODUCTS.md](/docs/quest/meta-products) | Each Meta product and its job |
| [JUDGE-PLAYBOOK.md](/docs/quest/judge-playbook) | An 8-minute path through the live demo |
| [PITCH-SCRIPT.md](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/docs/quest/PITCH-SCRIPT.md) | The spoken script. The early game-first [PITCH.md](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/docs/archive/quest/PITCH.md) was archived on 2026-11-04. |
| [BUSINESS.md](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/docs/quest/BUSINESS.md) | Who it is for and who else is out there |
