<!-- https://docs.arya.teamnightshift.org/docs/quest/game-design -->

# Game design

## Core loop

**Plan → find → grab → snap the receipt.** The grocery list is the quest
log. The real store is the dungeon. The items on their real shelves are
the treasures. Mobile first. The keyboard is for the demo only.

## My rules (2026-10-28)

- No lives, no game over, no clock, no way to lose. Points only go up.
- Dopamine during the hunt and after it, never stress or pressure.
- Upgrade the existing hunt; no separate game.
- The game must keep feeding four things: community shortage reports,
  store layout and shelf maps, consumption and spend from receipts and
  list completion (plus receipts for returns), and fun with kids or a
  partner.

## Plan a hunt

1. **Pick the store.** Each store says what you usually buy there,
   counted from your receipts ("my milk is from TJ, eggs from Costco").
2. **Move items into the quest.** The Arya list, sorted for that
   store. Items usually bought here, and new items, start ticked. Items
   usually bought elsewhere stay on the list. Usuals not on the list
   are suggested. ✕ removes an item from the list (Undo). Typed extras
   join the list. Planning is list management, not a second list.
3. **Check my list** appears only when Arya has a question.
4. A quest starts. Express, the plain-checklist mode, has no entry point
   any more; see Modes below.

## The hunt (Quest)

- One store view, picked by the store: real photos of a mapped store
  (people pixelated by SAM), shelf cards anywhere else.
- The next-item card suggests a stop; any stop can be grabbed in any
  order. A fresh shopper photo shows the item boxed when one exists.
- **Find it for me:** the camera scans for that one item. SAM 3.1
  boxes candidates and Muse Spark checks each crop. The item lights up
  and one tap grabs it. A miss never says the item is not there.
- Tools: Scan shelf, Not here?, How to
  play (?), sound.
- Put back any grab; nothing finishes by itself.
- I'm done shopping works any time. Leftovers are saved for the next trip or dropped. Nothing counts as failure.
- How to play shows once, on the first Quest hunt on a phone.

## Rewards

| Event | Reward |
| --- | --- |
| Grab | +10, the chip bumps, a fun fact |
| Combo count | Combo: each grab of the suggested stop adds 1. It never resets and put back never lowers it. |
| Boss | +40, only when the boss item was grabbed; a boss is an item you reported missing here on 2 earlier trips. |
| Halfway, full haul | milestone; full haul +25 and confetti |
| Receipt snapped | +50; the trip's points bank |
| Level line crossed | level-up moment (L2 at 100, L3 at 300, L4 at 600, +100 more each level) |

Sound and buzz are opt-in, off by default. Express stays quiet.
Offline grabs queue on the phone and sync when the signal returns.

## Modes

Quest was designed with a second mode, Express: the same list as a
plain checklist in walking order, with no points. Express no longer has
an entry point (see `STATUS.md`); its screen stays only for runs that
started before. The list works without Quest, and shopping from the
list needs no game.

Quest is a mood, not an age. With a child holding the phone, the kid
hunts and grabs while the adult handles quantities and checkout.

## Store drift: Spotter

Every hunt is a shelf survey. A grab proves a product is there; "Not
here?" (Empty shelf / Something else here / Can't tell, optional photo)
says it is not. A report edits nothing. It flags the stop and opens a
window. A later grab at the stop means a stockout. A second player
finding it elsewhere means a move, applied as a shelf-graph edit.
Find it for me sightings add the same signal.

Points on truth, never on reports: +2 for a true stockout, +10 for a
verified move. Eagle Eye badge (1 / 10 / 50 verified spots), Store
Guardian per store. Status only, never cash.

## Community

Every metric is receipt-verified: the receipt is the referee.

- **Boards:** Fastest Hands, Clean Sweep, Top Contributor, Big Haul,
  World Mapper, Globetrotter.
- **Badges:** Egg Baron, Banana Republic, Dairy Royalty, Midnight
  Shopper, Speed Demon, Return Regret, First Mapper, Perfect Week.
- **Races:** Shop-Off (first verified receipt wins), Split the List
  (not built), Clue Hunt (rollout).
- **Friends:** handle-based; no chat, no DMs, no lists shared. Run
  notifications are designed (Discussion 24), not built.
- Handles, never real names. Household boards are private. Spend boards
  are opt-in.

## Contribution

Store videos earn permanent first-mapper credit. Receipts stay
private; their reward is a smarter list and a hunt that plans itself.

## Never

- No random spawns or sponsored placements in routes.
- No purchases, external links or chat in the hunt.
- No pictures of people kept: frames are kept only after SAM pixelates
  the people it detects.

---

<!-- https://docs.arya.teamnightshift.org/docs/quest/map-my-store -->

# Map my store ("Teach Arya your store"): design

Me, 2026-10-28: replace "take a photo or record a video" with a guided
mapper. Map only the aisles you use, over many visits. Many partial maps
merge into one store map. A "not found" or "map is outdated" asks for one
specific capture. The engine keeps the best images.
Wireframe (v2): `docs/quest/map-my-store-wireframe.html`. Code: `api/storemap.py`,
`assistant/web/src/screens/Mapper.tsx`.

## Coverage model
A **segment** is one side of one aisle, or one wall or freezer run. A store
map is its list of segments. Shoppers add segments ("Add an aisle"). No store
starts seeded: the old Trader Joe's walkthrough seed was removed (2026-10-29),
and a saved section that only had a walkthrough baseline is dropped on load.

Status of a segment, from its best capture:
- **unmapped**: no capture, no baseline.
- **mapped**: best capture is 60 days old or less and no open flag.
- **aging**: best capture older than 60 days.
- **stale**: a "not found" or "outdated" flag is newer than the best capture.

Coverage is mapped segments over known segments. The denominator grows as
people add aisles, so the bar means "of what is known so far".

## Capture prompts
`next_prompt()` returns one capture: kind, title, why, numbered steps, time.
Order of need: stale, then unmapped, then aging. The shopper's **focus**
("Mine" aisles, saved per account) is served first. Two or more unmapped
segments in one zone get one **walk** prompt (about 20 s, the phone sends its
6 sharpest of 12 sampled frames as photos; no video upload). Otherwise a
**photo** prompt (about 10 s). A stale prompt names the missing item.

## How contributions merge
One shared file per store (platform plane, like the stores directory).
Segments merge on `zone_key`: "Aisle 4", "aisle #4 - Pasta" are one zone;
other labels merge on normalized words, minus a trailing "shelf". Each
segment keeps its 3 best captures. Contributors are stored as a hash, never
the username. Demo visitors write to their sandbox overlay, never the shared
map.

## Framing (me, 2026-10-28)
The shopper teaches Arya so Arya can help them: "Arya knows 64% of
Trader Joe's", and every capture says what it unlocks for you (a real
shelf photo in your next hunt). Helping other shoppers is the bonus.

## Capture: no retakes, ever
I said: "I click pictures, then app says not good... this will cause
friction." So the shopper opens a live camera and the app does the work:
- **Photo:** the phone grades every frame (sharpness, light), shows one
  live hint ("Hold still…", "A bit dark. Face the shelf light."), and
  snaps the best frame after 1.5 s steady, or the best seen by 6 s.
- **Walk:** the sharpest frame of every 2 s is kept; no video upload.
- The server never refuses a shot. A weak one is kept as a **partial**
  (`weak: true`). The segment stays "aging", the next better capture
  replaces it, and the engine asks again on a later visit.
- If the people scrub fails, nothing is kept and the app says "No need
  to redo it." It never asks for a retake.
- Without a live camera (old browser, permission denied) the system
  camera is the fallback, under the same rules.

## Splitting a long aisle
The walk's length decides: about 8 s of walking per section, 1 to 6
sections. The app calls `POST /api/storemap/split` and spreads the
walk's frames over the sections in time order (front / middle / back,
or first half / second half). Parts keep the zone key, so sightings and
"not found" reports still find them. A split is idempotent, so a second
shopper walking the same aisle fills the same sections. Old whole-aisle
captures are dropped on split; the walk that caused it fills the parts.

## When Arya asks
- **After a hunt:** one skippable card on the score screen ("Got 20
  seconds? Teach Arya Aisle 4. +10"). `GET /api/storemap/next?items=`
  puts an aisle where something on today's list was seen first. "Not
  now" mutes the store for 7 days (on the phone).
- **Can't find it:** a photo attached to the "Not here" report is
  ingested straight into the flagged section (no extra screen). Without
  one, the toast offers "Open camera". An item with no known aisle asks
  "Which aisle are you in?" as one tap.

## Rewards (no pressure)
+10 for a section that becomes mapped, +3 for a refresh or
confirmation. Titles: Scout 1, Pathfinder 5, Cartographer 15, Store
whisperer 40 sections. Each capture shows the store going from a% to
b% and the sections to the next 25% step. Credit is per account
(`map_credit.json`); nothing is ever taken away, and there are no
streaks or timers.

## How the engine chooses frames
All deterministic, $0, except two model calls per upload in the route:
SAM 3.1 people scrub (fails closed) and "grocery shelf" boxes for fill
(summed over bays, measured on the scrubbed JPEG).
1. Grade: sharpness (Laplacian variance), exposure (mean grey level),
   shelf fill. A weak frame is kept as a partial, never refused.
2. Score = 0.5 sharpness + 0.3 exposure + 0.2 fill (fill is neutral if the
   check failed).
3. Value = score x freshness; freshness halves every 30 days.
4. Same view as a kept capture (dhash distance 6 or less) is a
   **confirmation**: it refreshes the old capture's date, and swaps the image
   only if clearly sharper (+0.05). That clears a stale flag.
5. Keep the top 3 by value. The best one is shown for that segment.

## Refresh loop
`POST /api/storemap/outdated` or a "Not here" report marks a segment stale.
For an item, the segment is where the item was last seen (`note_sighting`
from Find it for me). If unknown, the item is parked as unplaced and the
shopper is asked which aisle they are in. The report response carries
`map_task`; the app offers "Take the photo".

## Privacy
Only scrubbed frames are kept. No opt-in screens yet (deferred by me
for the hackathon). Raw frames never touch disk.

## Not built yet
Item-level locations from captures (Muse Spark labels); automatic
`resolved` transitions for reports; stale flags expiring when no one
confirms; mapping silently from Find it for me frames during a hunt.

---

<!-- https://docs.arya.teamnightshift.org/docs/guide/agent-connector -->

# The agent connector (MCP)

Arya does not compete with the list apps and notes you already use.
It collects from them. The collection point is your own assistant.
Any MCP-capable agent connects to Arya once, with your account token.
From then on, anything you capture anywhere (a note, a reminder,
a chat message, an email receipt) can become part of your Arya list.
Your assistant can then answer from Arya's model instead of a stale
note.

Arya's list is the shared list: the one place the pattern engine can
compute on. Other apps are doors in and mirrors out, never a second
source of truth.

## Connect

I tested this on my own Muse (2026-11-02), with no terminal and no settings
file. I asked the Muse agent to connect to Arya. It asked for the code, opened
a secure connector-credentials vault for me to paste it into, and the
connection worked. The code never goes in the chat.

1. In Arya, open More → Settings → About Arya → Use Arya in Muse and tap "Make my
   code". Copy it. It is shown once and starts with `arya_`. A new code
   replaces the old one. (The token works with any MCP client, not just Muse.)
2. In your AI app, ask it to connect to Arya at
   `https://arya.teamnightshift.org/api/mcp`. When it asks for your code,
   paste it into the app's secure credentials step, never into the chat.
   Apps that take a server list instead use transport streamable HTTP
   (stateless; one POST per message) and the header
   `Authorization: Bearer <your code>`.
3. Ask it "What is on my Arya list?" Then try "Add oat milk to my Arya
   list" and "What am I running low on in Arya?" The new item also shows on
   the Lists screen in Arya.
4. If it says it cannot connect, make a new code (the old one stops working)
   and paste it into the vault again. Tap "Turn off this code" in Arya to
   switch the connection off.

The token acts as your account. It is accepted on the MCP door and on
the app's routes under `/api`, but never on `/auth` (it cannot mint tokens
or delete the account). A short list of routes is closed to tokens and
answers 403: calls that spend model credits in bulk (chat, photo and
shelf reads, avatars, the judge), groups, friends, push, feedback,
settings changes, price sharing, account export and receipt delete
through the app (`ARYA_TOKEN_GUARDS`). Revoke it from
the same screen at any time; minting a new one replaces the old.

### Backup: the Muse Code settings file

Only if the agent flow above is not available. Muse Code reads remote MCP
servers from `~/.config/muse/settings.json` (per the Meta docs at
dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/extending; not yet run end to end). Put the code in
an environment variable so it is not typed into a file or chat
(`read -rs ARYA_TOKEN; export ARYA_TOKEN`), then add:

```json
"mcp_servers": { "arya": { "transport": "streamable_http",
  "url": "https://arya.teamnightshift.org/api/mcp",
  "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${ARYA_TOKEN}" } } }
```

Keep `"schema_version": 1` in the file. Run `muse` from the same terminal
window and type `/mcp` to see the six tools.

## Limits

- 600 calls per account per hour (`ARYA_MCP_RATE`), shared by the connector,
  the Lists API (`docs/API.md` in the repo root) and every other route a token
  reaches; over it, 429 with `Retry-After`. 256 KB per request,
  50 items per `add_items`, 200 lines per `file_receipt`.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `get_snapshot` | Running-low items, spend and returns totals, trip count, top items. |
| `get_list` | The current shopping list, with quantities, check-offs and each item's list, plus the names of all lists. |
| `add_items` | Add items by name, as a person would say them, to a named list (`list`). Returns the items added and that list after the add. |
| `check_item` | Check an item off (or uncheck it) by name. |
| `file_receipt` | File a receipt the agent has already read. Arya verifies the arithmetic, files the lines, and learns from them; it spends no perception tokens of its own. |
| `get_receipts` | Recent filed receipts: merchant, date, total. |

Every item goes on a named list. The account's list names come up front, in the `initialize` instructions and in the `add_items` description from `tools/list`, so an agent asks "which list?" once instead of learning the names from a failed add. With one list, adds go there. The Lists API (`/api/v1`, see `docs/API.md`) is list-aware: it reads and writes each list by id.

## The showcased client

Muse Spark is the reference client. In chat, "add oat milk to my
list" files through `add_items`, "what am I low on?" answers from
`get_snapshot`, and a receipt photo read in chat files through
`file_receipt`. The protocol is the standard one. Nothing in the
connector is specific to a single assistant.

---

<!-- https://docs.arya.teamnightshift.org/docs/glossary -->

# Glossary

The words Arya uses, in plain terms. Names in quotes are the exact words on screen.

## In the app

- **Today**: the first tab. What is running low, store alerts and what to use soon. You can change what it shows with Customize your "Today" screen.
- **Navigation tab**: the row of tabs at the bottom of the phone: Today, Spending, Quest, Ask and More. "Customize navigation tab" changes which ones sit there.
- **Lists**: under More, one card per store list, with suggestions underneath. Every item sits on one list.
- **Suggestions**: items Arya thinks you may need, each with a reason. Arya never adds to a list by itself. You tap Add.
- **Running low**: staples that are due again, worked out from how often you buy them.
- **Use soon**: food you bought that should be eaten soon. "Used it" moves an item back to Suggestions.
- **Ask Arya**: the chat, on the tab named "Ask". Ask how to do something in Arya, or about your lists and spending.
- **Help tab**: the ask box, first steps, a how-to topic for each feature, and links to the Arya guide, Arya's powers, the Tour and Send feedback.
- **Arya**: a grocery app that learns how you shop from your receipts and helps shoppers help each other.
- **Arya guide**: the swipeable cards that explain each feature.
- **Tour**: the first-run walk-through, shown as bubbles over a dark screen.
- **Quest**: the optional game. It turns a shopping trip into a hunt through a model of your store and ends on a photo of your receipt. It has no clock and no way to lose.
- **Use Arya in Muse**: the Settings, About Arya row that connects the Muse assistant to your Arya account through the MCP connector.
- **Demo Town**: the simulated neighborhood of invented stores the demo household shops in. It is labelled as simulated.

## How it works

- **Model proposes, code checks**: a model reads the receipt. Plain code then checks every line against the printed total before anything posts.
- **Staple judge**: decides whether an item is a staple you buy again and again. Muse Spark is the main seat and Muse Spark Open a second seat.
- **Curator**: proposes product merges and splits for you to apply.
- **Crowd map**: the aisle layout built from shoppers' own store scans.
- **MCP connector**: lets an AI assistant add items and read lists through Arya's MCP endpoint.
- **Lists API**: a small bearer-token API to read and write your lists from a script. See the API reference.
- **PWA**: a web app you add to your phone's home screen. Arya is a PWA only.

## The Meta models

Model ids, jobs and measured numbers live in [the model map on the judges page](/docs/judges#which-model-does-which-job). This list only explains the words.

- **Muse Spark**: reads receipt photos first, and also runs the staple judge, the Curator, Ask Arya and photo reading. Arya uses the Standard tier.
- **Muse Wonder**: re-reads a receipt only when the arithmetic checks flag it, or when Spark fails.
- **SAM 3.1**: finds shelves and signs in a store scan, boxes items for Find it for me and pixelates the people it detects.
- **Muse Voice Transcribe**: turns speech into text for the list mic and Ask Arya.
- **Muse Image**: made the grab-celebration characters in Quest, once.
- **Muse Spark Open**: the open-weights model, hosted on Baseten. It is the second seat of the staple judge and sees item names only (no prices, dates, stores or account details).
- **Meta Model API**: the one client every server call goes through, with a daily spend ceiling.

## Not live

Community prices, Deals and Arya shoppers (seeing other shoppers nearby) are not live. Muse Glimmer is not used. Muse Code, running Muse Wonder, wrote the first version of the engine. It is not part of the shipped app.

---

<!-- https://docs.arya.teamnightshift.org/docs/architecture/design-decisions -->

# Design decisions, and what comes next

I built Arya as one well-defended single-server app on purpose. The window was for the product, not for a fleet of servers. This page has three parts: what is built and holds up for a few dozen people at once, what I know is weak, and the plan to grow past that. The dated choices are in the [decision log](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/docs/DECISIONS.md), what was made and when is on the [build page](/docs/what-we-built), and the unbuilt ideas are in the [roadmap](/docs/roadmap). What runs today is in [Architecture](/docs/architecture/overview).

## What is built?

- **Code does money, timing and lists at no model cost.** The ledger, patterns and derived list are rebuilt from the receipts, with no model involved, so they cannot drift. Every model call goes through one module that enforces the personal-data rule. (Architecture 0.3, 0.4)
- **Safe writes on one box.** Atomic JSON writes, a per-file lock, a per-request memo, and a full Postgres copy of every account document on the live site. (Architecture 0.5)
- **Layered spend control.** A daily ceiling for the app, a separate one for the demo, a per-visit share, per-account monthly and hourly limits, and an Ops switch to pause paid reads or change the photo reader without a deploy. Every call writes a ledger row. ([Model policy](/docs/architecture/model-policy))
- **Background work that survives a restart.** Receipt batches and store scans keep a pending list on disk and resume after a deploy.
- **Live sync that already spans processes.** Shared-list changes use Postgres `LISTEN/NOTIFY`, one listener per process. (Architecture 0.8)
- **A demo that cannot touch real data.** Each visit writes to an in-memory sandbox with a size cap.
- **Security basics.** Hashed session and token secrets, a strict script CSP, upload caps at the proxy, throttled sign-in, and people pixelated out of shelf photos before anything is stored.
- **Measured.** A [scale simulator](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/assistant/docs/SCALE-SIM.md) and a read-only performance pass on 2026-11-02. The Today screen takes about 65 ms alone, about 1.1 s with 10 people at once and about 4 s with 30. That was on a development machine, not the live server.

## What do I know is weak?

These are the findings from my own architecture audit of 2026-11-01 that still hold. Each is tied to a phase of the [scalability design](/docs/architecture/scalability). Two audit items are already closed: `/health` reports the running commit, and the photo reader is Spark first (see the [model map](/docs/judges#which-model-does-which-job)). That second change took the cost pressure off receipt batches.

| What | Why it matters | Fixed in |
|---|---|---|
| One process, one interpreter lock, no cap on model reads in the request thread pool | A burst of photo reads can slow pages that never call a model | Phases 4 and 6 |
| The spend guard reads the whole ledger file on each paid call; password sign-in hashes on the event loop | Both block other requests while they run, and the ledger grows with use | Phase 2 for the ledger; the hashing is not in the plan yet |
| Spend checks are "check, then spend", with no reservation | Parallel reads can overshoot a limit | Phase 6 |
| The ledger is an estimate from a price table, never reconciled with the provider's console | What Arya thinks it spent and what was billed can differ | Not in the plan yet; a manual weekly check |
| Postgres mode stores documents whole, with no version column or pool | Two processes could lose an update silently | Phase 2, before any second process |
| Sessions, demo visits, rate buckets and the receipt queue live in memory or files | A deploy drops every demo visit | Phases 3 and 5 |
| One worker reads every account's receipt batch in order; no cap on batches parked on disk | One big import makes the next person wait | Phase 5 |
| Store-map photos are base64 in one JSON file rewritten per photo | The first wall the simulator found | Phase 7 |
| Saves mirror the whole document to Postgres inside the request | A slow database slows a list tick | Phase 1 |
| `restore.sh` wipes the data folder before extracting; the off-site backup is set up by hand | A bad archive or a lost VM could lose data | Phase 0 |
| Tests run in CI only on demand (my choice, to keep the loop fast) | A broken merge can reach the server unless someone runs the suite | Not a scaling item; revisit after judging |
| Concurrency rules are by convention (each writer must remember the lock) | Easy to get wrong as more people touch the code | Phase 2 |

## What is the plan to grow it?

[Scalability design](/docs/architecture/scalability) has nine phases (0 to 8, the numbers the table above uses). Each phase is switched on by settings. Each has a rollback and a number to measure:

0. Baseline: request timing, a metrics endpoint and a live load test.
1. Hot cache: a short-lived cache, and the Postgres mirror off the request path.
2. Postgres master: Postgres as the master copy, with versioned updates.
3. Shared short-lived state: sessions, demo visits and rate buckets in a shared store.
4. Several processes.
5. Queue and workers: a job queue for receipt, scan and reminder jobs.
6. Model gateway: concurrency caps and spend reservation.
7. Object storage for photos.
8. Cloud provider.

Versioned writes come before a second process, and nothing runs before judging ends. It is a plan, not a promise.

---

<!-- https://docs.arya.teamnightshift.org/docs/architecture/overview -->

# Arya architecture (as built)

Status: living document, revised 2026-11-04. Section 0 is the one-page map with the diagram. Sections 1 to 13 are the design record. SPEC.md states the product rules. This document states
how the built system is put together. Where the two disagree, SPEC.md
wins for behavior and this document wins for structure.

## 0. The whole app on one page

![Arya architecture diagram](/repo/assistant/docs/architecture.svg)

*The diagram is `assistant/docs/architecture.svg` (plain SVG, light and dark),
redrawn and checked against `main` on 2026-11-04. The sections below say what
each box does. Their facts are checked against `main` on 2026-11-04, except the
live-site values in §0.11 and §10, which come from the Ops screen.*

**In one paragraph.** A phone-first PWA (React, built with Vite) talks
to one FastAPI process, which also serves the built app at `/`. Caddy fronts it with TLS. Code does the
money, timing and list logic at $0. Meta models read photos, judge
staples and answer questions, and every call to them goes through one
module (`api/meta_client.py`). State is one JSON document per area, kept
on a Docker volume, in Supabase Postgres, or both.

### 0.1 Front end (`assistant/web/`)

- React 19 and TypeScript, built by Vite into `web/dist`. The API serves
  the build at `/` and the static folder `assistant/pwa/` (images, store
  models, three.js, `scene.js`, the manifest, icons) beside it; the build
  wins on a name clash. `index.html` and `sw.js` are sent with
  `Cache-Control: no-cache`. The old address `/next/...` answers 302 to
  the same path at `/`.
- One screen per file in `web/src/screens/`, listed in
  `screens/registry.tsx`. Navigation is a stack (`app/nav.tsx`); the
  session (user, demo, currency, language) is `app/session.tsx`. Shared
  parts: `web/src/ui/` (sheet, toast, info sheet, the store view) and
  `web/src/lib/` (API calls, formats, stores, language).
- The hunt, Express, Pack, haul, album, share, mapper, group live sync
  (`app/groupLive.ts`), push reminders, powers and the install prompt
  are ported one to one from the old plain-JS files. The store view is
  `scene.js` (three.js), loaded as a classic script.
- The navigation tab is **Today**, **Spending**, **Quest**, **Ask** and **More**
  (the default; it can be customized). More holds Lists, Receipts, Stores, Help
  and Settings. Settings opens the Profile page (Group, Preferences with
  Reminders, Account, About Arya, Sign out last). About Arya is the `about`
  view: Arya's powers, Use Arya in Muse, Add to Home Screen, Keeping Arya
  running. (Updated 2026-11-02, #416; this replaced the earlier six-tab layout.)
- Service worker `web/src/sw.js`, built to `/sw.js` (vite-plugin-pwa,
  injectManifest). It precaches the built shell and the runtime files of
  the static folder. It is network first. It sends `/api/`, `/auth/`,
  `/decode`, `/import` and `/eyes` straight to the network, never touches
  a write (non-GET) or the live stream `/api/group/live`, and shows push
  reminders. It takes control at once and deletes every other cache,
  the old `arya-v*` caches too.
- Security: no inline script (the CSP has `script-src 'self'`;
  `tests/test_csp.py` checks `web/index.html`); no inline handlers.
- Tests: string pins in `assistant/tests/` (they read `web/src` through
  `tests/frontend.py`), vitest tests beside the code
  (`web/src/**/*.test.ts*`), and browser runs in `web/e2e/`.
- Style: light theme, greyscale structure and one orange accent; see
  `DESIGN.md`.

### 0.2 API (`assistant/api/`)

`api/main.py` is a short file: the app, the `require_login` middleware,
a handler that turns a model failure (`RuntimeError`) into a 502 with a
plain sentence, `/health`, one ordered router list, the Lists API mounted
at `/api/v1`, and the static mount for the PWA. Routes live in `api/routes/`, one router per area:

| Router | What it serves |
|---|---|
| `auth`, `account` | sign-in, registration (closed unless `ARYA_REGISTRATION_OPEN=1`; the Ops flag overrides the env, and sign-up is closed on the live site), email code (Supabase) and Google (Arya's own sign-in, flagged), connector and Lists API token, settings, export, feedback, push opt-in |
| `intake`, `review`, `receiptjobs` | receipt photo, PDF, text, order text, structured JSON, Costco JSON, voice transcribe, Curator, review queue; receipt batches that keep reading while the app is closed |
| `lists`, `items`, `expiry` | named lists, add by text or photo, check, move, judge runs, item pages and flags, expiry dates |
| `home`, `chat` | the Today payload, Ask Arya and its apply step |
| `prices` | own-receipt prices, Analysis insights, Arya's powers |
| `groups` | shared home: create, invite, join, leave, live stream |
| `quest`, `questmap`, `receipts`, `shelf`, `storemap`, `stores`, `eyes`, `avatar`, `friends` | hunts, filing items into a store's zones, receipts with originals, shelf scan, Map my store, store directory, pantry and shelf photos kept as sightings, avatar, friends |
| `mcp_connector` | `/api/mcp`, the tool surface for a Muse agent |
| `lists_v1` (mounted at `/api/v1`) | the Open Lists API: read and write your own lists from another app, bearer token only, its own error format |
| `ops` | the owner's Ops screen: models, limits, accounts, freezes, Ask locks (owner only) |
| `town` | Demo Town routes; the demo account only, and only when `ARYA_DEMO_TOWN=1` |

Older siblings stay beside the package: `album_routes`, `hunt_routes`,
`haul_routes`, `pack`. Shared plumbing is in `api/deps.py` (cost ledger,
budget guard, `new_client()`, rate-limit buckets, JSON helpers),
`api/demo_guard.py` (login middleware, demo sandbox, door caps, the list of
routes a token cannot reach), `api/ask_guard.py` (the Ask input and output
guard and its three-strike lock, §6) and `api/settings.py` with
`api/site_flags.py` (a value set in Ops, then the env var, then the default).

### 0.3 Engines in code ($0)

`decode/service.py` (PDF text layer, scanned PDF pages rendered with
`pypdfium2` and sent to the photo reader, arithmetic reconcile),
`ledger/` (returns netted FIFO, allocations), `patterns/` (cadence and
price by store), `list/` (the derived list and its reasons),
`state.running_low` (one rule for Today and Ask), `prices.py` (see §0.7),
`expiry.py`, `dictionary/`, `optimizer.py` (merges duplicate adds and fixes typos before a hunt) and `cart/` (a sandbox cart proposal; approval is a state change only, and the app no longer shows it).

### 0.4 Models

All calls go through `api/meta_client.py`; the personal-data rule is
enforced there. `open_client.py` is the only other model client.

| Job | Model | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Reasoning, decode fallback, judge, Curator, Eyes, Ask Arya | `muse-spark-1.3` (Standard; `ARYA_SPARK_TIER=contributor` is an operator option, off) | cached prefixes, low effort |
| Receipt photo reader (default, `auto`) | Spark first; `muse-wonder-1.0` (90 s bound) re-reads only a receipt the arithmetic checks flag | `decoded_by` records which read was kept; `ARYA_PHOTO_READER=spark` or `wonder`, or the Ops "Photo reader" switch, changes it with no code change |
| Celebration characters, generated once | `muse-image-1.0` | |
| Voice in | `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0` | |
| Shelf and people segmentation | `sam-3.1` | people SAM detects are pixelated first, and the frame is discarded if that fails (detection is not perfect and has not been scored) |
| Second judge seat, dictionary enrichment | Spark Open, hosted on Baseten | platform data only; the client refuses personal data |

### 0.5 Storage

`api/state.py` keeps one JSON document per former file (receipts,
dictionary, flags, lists, quest, push...). `ARYA_STORE` picks the
backend: `json` (default; files under `data/users/<account>/`),
`dual` (files are the truth, each save mirrors to Postgres) or `pg`
(Supabase table `arya.user_docs`, keyed by owner and document name,
role `arya_app`, via `DATABASE_URL`). The demo account always uses files,
and its visitors write only to an in-memory sandbox overlay. Caches and
big blobs (`shelf_matches.json`, `storemap_img.json`) stay on disk in
every mode. A receipt's original photo or PDF is kept per account.

### 0.6 Auth

Password accounts (PBKDF2 hashes, throttled sign-in, cookie sessions
whose tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes). Account names allow only
letters, digits and `. _ % + - @`. Email-code sign-in goes through Supabase
Auth and Google sign-in is Arya's own (`api/google_oauth.py`, used when
`GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` are set; otherwise
Google goes through Supabase). Either way the provider only proves an email
address; Arya keeps its own account and cookie (`api/supabase_auth.py`, flag
`ARYA_SUPABASE_AUTH`). The Muse connector and the Lists API use a bearer
token whose hash is stored.

### 0.7 Price intelligence

`api/prices.py` is deterministic and uses only the household's own
receipts: per-store unit prices, a cheaper-store hint when the gap is
real, a trend only with enough buys over enough days, the household's own
basket inflation, a split-the-list suggestion, food waste in dollars.
Nothing is fetched from a store, a flyer, an API or the web. Ask Arya
answers price questions from these precomputed facts. Community prices,
Deals and Arya Shoppers are opt-in, recorded only, and not live.

### 0.8 Groups and live sync

With `ARYA_GROUPS=1` (on in compose), an account in a group reads and
writes the shared stores (lists, flags, product knowledge) in the group's
plane; receipts stay with the account that filed them and every member
sees them. Invites are a 6-letter code valid 48 hours. Leaving copies
the lists. Live sync: every shared save calls `live.changed(group_id)`;
each open app holds one Server-Sent Events stream (`/api/group/live`)
and reloads when its group changes. With `DATABASE_URL` set the change is
a Postgres `NOTIFY arya_group` and one listener thread per process wakes
its streams; without it, or with `ARYA_LIVE_PG=0`, the wake stays
in-process.

### 0.9 Push reminders

Flag `ARYA_PUSH_REMINDERS=1` plus VAPID keys. A phone opts in from
Settings; the subscription is saved in `push.json`. A daily cron line
runs `python -m api.reminders`, which sends at most one push per account
per day for staples that run out inside the notice window. No model
calls. Steps: `PUSH-REMINDERS.md`.

### 0.10 Deploy

One Oracle VM, Docker Compose with two services: `api` (uvicorn,
`deploy/Dockerfile.api`) and `caddy` (TLS, security headers, CSP, plain
HTTP redirects to HTTPS). Data lives in the `arya-data` volume. Settings
come from `deploy/.env` (VM only); compose lists every variable the app
reads, and `tests/test_compose_env.py` fails if one is missing. Deploy is
`git pull` then `docker compose up -d --build` in `assistant/deploy`
(`deploy.sh`); never rsync `--delete`. The api image builds the app
(`web/`) in a node stage and copies `web/dist` in. `backup.sh` and `restore.sh`
handle the nightly backup. CI is manual only
(`.github/workflows/tests.yml`).

### 0.11 Feature flags and settings

Most limits and switches can also be set in the owner's Ops screen (Settings,
then Ops and health). A value set in Ops wins over the env var, which wins over
the code default. The table gives the default in compose. The live site (checked with Ops on
Nov 2) differs in these places: `ARYA_STORE=dual`; push reminders on (daily
cron at 13:00 UTC); Supabase Auth and email sign-in on; Demo Town on; the
Kroger aisle lookup on; own-key sign-up off; photo reader `auto`; Spark tier
`standard`; new sign-up closed (the Ops flag wins over the env). Budgets: $10 a
day for the app, $100 a day for the demo (code default $2), $2 per demo visit (code default $0.40).
Per-account limits are $3 heads-up, $20 monthly pause and $10 hourly freeze.

| Variable | Default in compose | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `ARYA_STORE` | `json` | `json`, `dual` or `pg` storage |
| `DATABASE_URL` | empty | Supabase Postgres connection (role `arya_app`) |
| `ARYA_GROUPS` | `1` | shared households (code default is off) |
| `ARYA_LIVE_PG` | `1` | live sync through Postgres NOTIFY when `DATABASE_URL` is set |
| `ARYA_PUSH_REMINDERS` | `0` | push reminders; needs `ARYA_VAPID_*` keys |
| `ARYA_SUPABASE_AUTH` | `0` | email code and Google sign-in; needs `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` |
| `ARYA_SUPABASE_SIGNUP` | `1` | `0` limits Supabase sign-in to existing accounts |
| `ARYA_REGISTRATION_OPEN` | `0` | open password sign-up |
| `ARYA_PHOTO_READER` | `auto` | receipt photo reader: `auto` (Spark first, Wonder on a flagged read), `spark` or `wonder` |
| `ARYA_DAILY_BUDGET_USD` | `10` | app model-spend ceiling per day |
| `ARYA_USER_HEAVY_MONTHLY_USD` | `3` | one account's month of AI spend that shows a heads-up on its usage screen |
| `ARYA_USER_MONTHLY_CEILING_USD` | `5` | one account's month of AI spend that pauses its paid reads until the 1st |
| `ARYA_USER_HOURLY_FREEZE_USD` | `1` | one account's hour of AI spend that switches its paid reads off for `ARYA_USER_FREEZE_HOURS` (24); I can lift it with `POST /api/usage/unfreeze` |
| `ARYA_COST_PUBLIC_MIN` | `50` | accounts with spend before the whole-Arya totals show on the usage screen |
| `ARYA_COST_PAID_BY` | `Hackathon credits` | who the usage screen says pays for the AI reading |
| `ARYA_DEMO_DAILY_BUDGET_USD` | `100` (code default `2`) | demo household's day bucket |
| `ARYA_DEMO_SESSION_BUDGET_USD` | `2.00` (code default `0.40`) | one demo visit's share |
| `ARYA_DEMO_DOOR_RATE`, `ARYA_DEMO_AUTH_RATE` | `240`, `120` | per-IP demo door and auth rate limits |
| `ARYA_FEEDBACK_DAILY_CAP` | `5` | feedback messages per account per day |
| `ARYA_TOKEN_GUARDS` | `on` | an API token cannot call the blocked routes (bulk model spend, groups, push, feedback, account export, Kroger aisle hints); `off` lifts the list |
| `ARYA_DEMO_TOWN` | `0` | demo household shops at simulated stores in a simulated neighborhood (`DEMO-TOWN.md`) |
| `ARYA_OWNER_USERNAME` | empty | the owner account: it runs Ops and health (models, limits, accounts, freezes, Ask locks, registration). The owner can hand the role to another account in Ops; the old owner keeps owner rights for 24 hours so a wrong pick can be undone |
| `ARYA_OPS_EMAIL`, `ARYA_ALERT_EMAIL`, `RESEND_API_KEY` | empty | email through Resend: delete-account codes, waitlist and feedback notes, and one alert per Ask lock (at most 20 a day); off until the key is set |
| `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` | empty | Arya's own Google sign-in; without both, Google goes through Supabase |
| `ARYA_SCAN_DAILY_FRAMES` | `120` | Map my store frames per account per day |
| `ARYA_KROGER_AISLES`, `KROGER_CLIENT_ID`, `KROGER_CLIENT_SECRET`, `ARYA_KROGER_DAILY_CALLS` | `0`, empty, empty, `800` | live Kroger aisle hint (api/kroger.py); never stored |
| `MODEL_API_KEY`, `BASETEN_API_KEY`, `ARYA_OPEN_MODEL`, `GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY` | empty | model keys and the store picker |

### 0.12 Cost guards

Every model call writes a row to the cost ledger. The app, the demo
household and each demo visit spend from separate buckets (§10). Live
doors, batch judge runs and hunt creation pass the guard first; the
demo's live doors also have per-IP caps. Deterministic code never calls a
model. An Ask message the guard refuses costs $0 (no model call), and
`max_tokens` bounds each Ask reply (§6).

## 1. The shape: two layers

Arya has two layers. Each layer does the work it is good at.

- **The edge** is the user's own Muse. It sees the media: receipt
  photos, PDFs, pasted orders. It reads them and sends
  Arya structured data only; on this path no receipt image reaches the
  server. A receipt photo filed in the app itself is kept per account
  and is viewable in the app ("View receipt", Discussion 42). This is
  an accepted trade-off, recorded in SPEC.md.
- **The core** is the Arya server. It verifies, remembers, reasons, and
  answers. It spends no tokens on reading media.

The rule between the layers: **the client proposes, Arya disposes.**
Client data is untrusted. Totals must reconcile in code before a receipt
is accepted. Low-confidence lines go to the review queue.

## 2. Intake paths

All paths end in one contract: a decoded receipt with lines, subtotal,
tax, and total.

1. **Structured intake (primary).** POST /api/intake/structured. The
   user's Muse posts the decoded receipt as JSON. The server recomputes
   every line status. A subtotal that does not match the lines fails
   reconciliation and is marked, never silently accepted.
2. **Order text.** POST /api/intake/order-text. A pasted online order
   (Instacart, Amazon) is extracted server-side, then follows the same
   path. Delivery fees and tips are excluded by rule.
3. **Server decode (fallback).** PDF text and photo decode endpoints
   remain for clients that cannot decode at the edge. They use the
   Model API under the model policy (MODEL-POLICY.md).
4. **Costco JSON export.** Bootstrap seed only. It is not a product
   intake path.

## 3. Verification in code (no model, no cost)

- Arithmetic: line totals must sum to the subtotal within 5 cents.
- Line status: auto at confidence 0.8 or above, else unverified and into
  the review queue.
- **Discount lines are structure, not identity.** A discount line
  (Costco prints it as "/<item number>") attaches to its parent item
  (named on the receipt, else the previous item line) and is always
  auto-verified. It never enters the review queue, on any path.
- Fee lines are classified once and never enter patterns or the list.

## 4. Identity: what things are

Three mechanisms, in order of strength.

1. **The dictionary** maps each store SKU to a canonical name. A name the
   user confirms teaches the dictionary. An item whose name cannot be
   established is **unresolved**: off the list, out of patterns, waiting
   in the review queue. Arya never guesses a name.
2. **Groups.** Products are grouped by an explicit group key when one is
   set, else by their normalized name. Costco re-SKUs the same product
   under one name; the group is the product everywhere it matters:
   patterns, ledger, list. Merges and splits set the explicit key.
3. **The Curator** (server-side reasoning) proposes merges and splits
   inside candidate clusters built in code at no cost. The model judges
   a cluster under a strict doctrine: same product only; never across
   organic vs conventional, form, flavor, fat content, or a size that
   makes a different product; when in doubt, keep separate. **A proposal
   changes nothing until the user applies it. No silent edits, ever.**
   Proposals the dictionary has already overtaken (members already one
   group, a duplicate, a split already in effect) retire automatically
   as *superseded* and are never shown.

## 5. The Resolver: research at the edge

Arya's server models have no web access. Identification from the outside
world is therefore an edge job, run by the user's Muse:

- Trigger: an unresolved dictionary item, or an unverified receipt line
  whose name is abbreviated or unreadable.
- Method: the retailer's own catalog first. A store item number matched
  on the retailer's site (for Costco: costco.com and its same-day
  storefront) is the strongest evidence. Then the wider web.
- Output: candidates **with source URLs**, posted to Arya
  (POST /api/review/suggest) and shown in the review queue next to the
  item or line. Research is evidence, not a verdict: the user settles
  with one tap, and settling teaches the dictionary.
- A brand initial alone is not evidence. Items with no catalog match
  stay open.

## 6. The reasoning agents in the core

Each agent has a narrow job and a named limit.

- **Staple judge.** Input: pattern facts only (buys, cadence, quantities,
  all computed in code). Output: STAPLE, SEASONAL, OCCASIONAL, ONE_OFF, or
  NOT_CONSUMABLE per product. The verdict gates admission to the list.
  Explicit user intent always beats the judge. Unjudged and unresolved
  items stay off the list.
- **Curator.** See §4. Proposes identity changes; never applies them.
- **Ask Arya.** Chat over a household snapshot. Actions (add to list,
  remove from list, ran out, mark expired, never suggest, snooze) are
  validated server-side. A list is found by a near name ("Costco" finds
  "Costcozy"), and only a row already on a list can be removed. The
  snapshot carries receipt facts (count, last, biggest, trips per
  store), spend per store per month, pack dates as words, and the
  cheapest store per item. Numbers come from the data, never from the
  model. At most 10 actions
  run in a turn. More than 3 removes in one turn wait for a yes (Yes, do these
  or Not now) on every screen. On the Ask tab the other actions apply at
  once; from a list or a hunt, adds apply with Undo and the riskier actions
  (out, expired, never, snooze) wait for a yes (`/api/chat/apply`). Demo
  sessions can chat; it is a live door under the demo's per-IP and per-visit
  caps (§10).
- **Ask guard** (`api/ask_guard.py`). The person's latest message is checked
  against high-confidence phrases only (an override with a target, a prompt
  leak, secrets, other accounts). A hit gets a fixed refusal with no model
  call, and counts a strike. Three strikes in 24 hours pause Ask: a demo visit
  for 24 hours, a real account until the owner unlocks it in Ops (the message says to email support). The owner is
  never locked. A reply that quotes the system prompt, holds something shaped
  like a key or links off Arya is swapped for the refusal, with no strike.
  Stored text (item and list names, the screen, a photo) never strikes. Each
  Ask reply is capped at 1,500 tokens.

## 7. Money rules (summary; SPEC.md owns the detail)

- Returns are first-class: FIFO netting against buys, refunds reconcile
  into spend, patterns count kept items only, a returned item is never
  re-suggested.
- Every line carries an allocation: HOUSEHOLD (default) or FOR-OTHERS.
  For-others spend is in the ledger, never in patterns, inventory, or
  the list.
- The list is a derived view of the inventory model, never the source
  of truth.

## 8. Accounts, tokens, and the connector

- Per-user state is a set of JSON documents, one per former file
  (receipts, dictionary, flags, lists, quest...). `ARYA_STORE` picks
  where they live: `json` (files under data/users/<account>/, the
  default), `dual` (files are the truth, every save is mirrored to
  Postgres), or `pg` (table `arya.user_docs`, see `api/pgstore.py`).
  The demo account always stays on files.
- An account name is also a folder name, so it holds only letters,
  digits and `. _ % + - @` (`auth.valid_name`). Passwords are PBKDF2
  hashes; sign-in is throttled; sessions are cookies, and session
  tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes.
- Email code sign-in (Supabase Auth) is built behind
  `ARYA_SUPABASE_AUTH=1`, off by default and on in the live site. Google
  sign-in is Arya's own (`api/google_oauth.py`) when its client id and secret
  are set, with the Supabase Google provider as the fallback. The provider only
  proves the email; Arya keeps its own account (named by the email, no
  password) and its own cookie (`api/supabase_auth.py`).
- A connector token is `arya_` plus a random secret. **Only its SHA-256
  hash is stored.** It is shown once at mint. Minting a new one replaces
  the old, and it can be revoked at any time. Bearer tokens are accepted
  alongside session cookies, and the same token works for the Lists API
  (`/api/v1`). A token cannot reach paid bulk reads, Ops, groups, push,
  export or the Kroger lookup (`demo_guard._TOKEN_BLOCKED`). Demo accounts
  cannot mint.
- The Muse connector (custom.arya) carries its own instruction doc:
  operations, when to file, the verification rules, the Resolver
  procedure, filing hygiene. **The doc is the standing prompt.** The
  user writes no prompt.
- Routing is contextual. A receipt, an order, or a question about the
  user's own list, spend, or inventory goes to Arya. A general question
  does not. "Arya, …" always routes. Ambiguous input: ask, or state
  the assumption.

## 9. Onboarding

1. Create an account. A new account opens on Today; there is no
   Connect an AI agent step on first run.
2. Connecting Muse is optional, from Settings > About Arya > Use Arya in Muse:
   make the code there (shown once).
3. Tell the Muse agent to connect to Arya; it asks for the code and opens a
   secure credentials vault. Paste the code there, never into a chat message.
4. Talk to Muse. The screen carries these steps and a copyable fallback setup
   prompt for assistant apps that do not load the connector doc automatically.
   The Muse Code settings-file route is the backup (`AGENT-CONNECTOR.md`).

## 10. Cost control

- MODEL-POLICY.md is normative: deterministic work in code at $0;
  Spark 1.3 Standard, low effort, cached prefixes for volume reasoning
  (if the Contributor operator option is on, a client-side 140
  requests/min gate applies; its limit is 150); Wonder is banned from
  volume paths.
- Every model call is written to a cost ledger. The app's daily
  ceiling (`ARYA_DAILY_BUDGET_USD`, $10) stops app model spend; the
  demo household spends from a separate bucket
  (`ARYA_DEMO_DAILY_BUDGET_USD`, $100/day in compose) and each demo visit from its
  own share (`ARYA_DEMO_SESSION_BUDGET_USD`, $2 in compose), so demo use cannot
  drain the app. Every live door, batch judge run and hunt creation
  passes the guard first.
- A model answer that cannot be read is a 502 with a plain sentence,
  never a 500 (`meta_client.parse_json`). Each account has its own limits:
  a monthly heads-up, a monthly pause on paid reads, and an hourly freeze (defaults
  $3, $5 and $1, see the flag table; the live site uses $3, $20 and $10, and the owner
  account is exempt), on top of the daily ceiling for the whole app.
- api/meta_client.py is the only module that calls the Model API. The
  personal-data rule is enforced there by construction.

## 11. Deployment

- One Oracle VM (Always Free; no new cloud resources). Docker Compose:
  the API and Caddy with Let's Encrypt. No database container: data is
  JSON files, mirrored to Supabase on the live site (`ARYA_STORE=dual`); after judging Postgres can become the master copy (`pg`). Public name:
  arya.teamnightshift.org (Cloudflare A record, DNS only). The old
  arya-pilot.duckdns.org name is a permanent Caddy redirect to it.
- Known limit: one uvicorn process on one VM. Demo sandboxes live in that
  process's memory and the JSON files have one writer, so it cannot run as
  several processes yet. Dual-mode saves mirror to Supabase inside the
  request, so a slow Supabase can slow a save. Roughly a few dozen people at
  once is the ceiling (README, Known limits). After judging: Postgres as
  master copy, session state out of memory, several processes, a cloud
  provider (see `docs/ROADMAP.md`; the phased design is
  `docs/SCALABILITY-DESIGN.md`, a plan, not built).
- Deploy is `git pull` on the VM, then a compose rebuild. Never
  rsync --delete: it once deleted the VM-only deploy environment.
- Settings come from `deploy/.env` (VM only). Compose passes only the
  variables it lists, so every setting the app reads is listed in
  `docker-compose.yml`; `tests/test_compose_env.py` fails if one is
  missing. `.env.example` names them.
- The full test suite runs before a PR merges. A GitHub Actions workflow
  (`.github/workflows/tests.yml`) runs it on demand only, not on
  every PR (my choice). Nothing is committed to `main` directly;
  a session log goes to `loops/` and `STATUS.md` is updated.

### 11.1 Logs and backups (VM runbook)

- **Log caps.** Compose caps each container's log at 5 files of 10 MB
  (`x-logging` in `docker-compose.yml`), so logs cannot fill the disk.
  The cap applies when a container is recreated: `docker compose up -d`.
- **Nightly backup.** `deploy/backup.sh` archives the data volume (and
  the `arya` Postgres schema when `ARYA_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL` is set in
  `deploy/.env`) into `~/arya-backups`, keeping the newest 7 of each.
  Install once on the VM with `crontab -e`:
  `17 3 * * * /path/to/arya/assistant/deploy/backup.sh >> /path/to/arya-backup.log 2>&1`
  Check it with `ls -l ~/arya-backups` the next morning.
- **Off-VM copy.** A backup on the same disk dies with the VM. Install
  rclone (`sudo apt install rclone`), run `rclone config` once to add a
  remote you own (Oracle Object Storage, Google Drive, any S3), then add
  `ARYA_BACKUP_REMOTE=<remote>:arya-backups` to `deploy/.env`. The script
  then copies each night's files there and exits non-zero (so the log
  shows it) if the copy fails.
- **Restore.** `deploy/restore.sh <arya-data-*.tar.gz>` stops the api,
  replaces the data volume and starts it again. The Postgres dump is
  restored by hand with `psql`.

## 12. Quest storage

Per account, in `quest.json`: sessions, Shop-Offs, friends, Spotter
reports, and sightings (item, store, shelf label, time; no image).
`shelf_frames.json` holds one fresh shelf photo per store and item,
already scrubbed of people by SAM (`shelfscan.scrub_people`; no scrub,
no frame). `GET /api/quest/plan` counts purchases per store from the
ledger for Plan a hunt ($0). The demo sandbox overlays all of it in
memory. The store directory (`stores.json`) is platform-level.

## 13. Not built / held

- A fixed per-account spend allowance that resets by itself. Not built; per-account
  limits do exist (§10: defaults $3 heads-up, $5 pause, $1 hourly freeze; live $3, $20, $10).
- Public registration is closed by default (`ARYA_REGISTRATION_OPEN`; the Ops flag overrides the env and is closed on the live site). The
  owner can open it in Settings. Every door runs on Meta models: Muse in
  chat, Spark on the Meta API in the app.
- Forgot-password: not built. Once switched on, email code sign-in
  (§8) lets a person in without a password.

---

<!-- https://docs.arya.teamnightshift.org/docs/architecture/scalability -->

# Scalability design

Status: a plan, not shipped. Nothing on this page is built unless it says
"today". Written 2026-11-02 against `main` after #489. It extends the
one-line plan in [`ROADMAP.md`](/docs/roadmap) ("Scale out as the community
grows") and the Known limits entry in the [README](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md#what-are-the-known-limits).
Where this page says more, it does not contradict them. No provider, dates
or costs are named. Each phase is chosen when the number of shoppers asks
for it.

One idea shapes every choice here: Arya is a community app that grows
with its users. The design keeps one codebase and one set of product rules
(`assistant/docs/SPEC.md`). The operator turns each phase on with
settings, one at a time, with a way back.

## 1. What runs today

One container, one process, one VM, as recorded in
[`assistant/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](/docs/architecture/overview) sections
0.5, 0.10 and 11.

```
phone (PWA)  --https-->  CDN / DNS proxy  --->  Caddy (TLS)  --->  uvicorn, 1 process
                                                                   |  FastAPI routes
                                                                   |  engines ($0 code)
                                                                   |  model client
                                                                   v
                                      data volume (JSON per account, photos, caches)
                                      Postgres on Supabase (mirror, ARYA_STORE=dual)
                                      Meta Model API, Baseten (model calls)
```

Where state lives today, and why each one matters for scale:

| State | Where it lives today | Shared across processes? |
|---|---|---|
| Account documents (receipts, lists, flags, quest, ...) | JSON files under `data/users/<account>/`, mirrored to `arya.user_docs` in Postgres (`dual`) | No: file locks are per process, mirror is write-only |
| Group documents | `data/groups/<id>/`, same mirror | No |
| Sign-in sessions | `sessions.json` plus a parsed copy in process memory | Through the file only |
| Demo sessions and sandboxes | Process memory (`auth._demo_sessions`, `demo_guard._demo_sandboxes`) | No |
| Rate-limit and door buckets | Process memory (`api/deps.py`, `api/demo_guard.py`) | No |
| Cost ledger | JSON lines file, scanned whole for "spent today" | Through the file only |
| Receipt originals, shelf frames, map images | Files on the data volume (`storemap_img.json` is rewritten per photo) | No |
| Receipt and scan jobs | One worker thread per process, pending list in a file | No |
| Group live sync | Postgres `NOTIFY arya_group` (one listener thread per process) | Yes, when `DATABASE_URL` is set |
| Push reminders | A daily cron line on the VM | n/a |

### 1.1 Bottlenecks, in the order they will bite

Measured numbers are from the read-only performance pass of 2026-11-02 on a
development machine with a 117-receipt account, not the live server (the
README says the same). The ordering below is a judgment, not a measurement.

1. **One process, one GIL.** The Today payload is computed in Python on each
   read (the derived list, ledger and patterns are rebuilt from receipts, with
   a per-request memo only). Alone it takes about 65 ms. With 10 people at
   once the median is about 1.1 s, and with 30 about 4 s. Threads share the
   interpreter, so more threads do not help. The fix is more processes,
   which the next three items block.
2. **Process memory holds visitor state.** Demo sessions, demo sandboxes
   and rate-limit buckets live in the process. A second process would not
   see a demo visitor's session. A restart drops every demo visit.
3. **Files have one writer.** `_file_lock` is a process-local lock. Two
   processes writing the same account's `lists.json` would race. Dual mode
   mirrors the whole document, so the mirror carries no version and
   cannot detect a lost update. `pg` mode (not live) is a whole-document
   read-modify-write with the same process-local locks.
4. **Saves wait for the mirror.** In `dual` mode each save upserts the whole
   document to Postgres inside the request thread (connect timeout 5 s, one
   retry). A slow database slows every tick on a list.
5. **Model calls share the request thread pool.** Reads of receipts, Ask and
   shelf scans run in the default thread pool beside sync routes. A burst of
   receipt reads can starve plain page loads, and provider rate limits are
   handled per call, not per app.
6. **Big blobs rewrite on every change.** `storemap_img.json` is rewritten per
   mapping photo; receipt originals live on one disk; the nightly backup
   is on the same disk unless `ARYA_BACKUP_REMOTE` is set.
7. **No shared cache.** The Today payload is recomputed per request. The
   per-request memo saves repeat work inside one request only.
8. **Observability is logs and `/health`.** There is a cost ledger and an ops
   digest, but no request timing, no queue depth and no alert.

## 2. Target architecture

The target is plain on purpose: stateless app processes behind a load
balancer, one database as the master copy, one shared store for short-lived
state, one queue for background work, and one object store for files. Every box
below is a role, not a product.

```
phone (PWA) --> CDN / edge cache (static shell, images)
                     |
                     v
              load balancer (TLS, health checks, sticky nothing)
                     |
        +------------+------------+------------+
        |            |            |            |
     app proc     app proc     app proc     app proc      (N identical, stateless)
        |            |            |            |
        +-----+------+-----+------+-----+------+
              |            |            |
              v            v            v
        Postgres        shared        queue        object storage
        (master copy,   key-value     (jobs,       (receipt originals,
        per-doc         store         reminders,   shelf frames, map
        versions,       (sessions,    model calls) images; private
        LISTEN/NOTIFY)  demo boxes,                buckets, signed URLs)
                        rate buckets,
                        hot cache)
                                      |
                                      v
                                 worker procs (same image, no HTTP)
                                      |
                                      v
                             model gateway (one place for
                             concurrency, retries, provider
                             rate limits, cost ledger rows)
                                      |
                                      v
                          Meta Model API, Baseten (unchanged)

        metrics + logs + traces from every box --> one dashboard, a few alerts
```

### 2.1 Stateless app processes

- Same container image as today, started with N processes behind the load
  balancer. A process keeps nothing between requests except read caches it
  can lose. Any process can serve any request, so a crash or a deploy takes
  one process out, not the site.
- Health check stays `/health`; the load balancer stops sending to a process
  that fails it. Rolling deploys replace processes one at a time, and the
  in-memory demo state no longer matters because it has moved out (2.3).
- Code change: none to routes. The seams already exist: `state._load/_save`,
  `auth.new_session/session_info`, `demo_guard._demo_sandbox`, `deps` rate
  buckets, `receiptjobs`/`scanjobs` queues, `live.changed`. Each gets a
  shared backend behind the same function names.

### 2.2 Postgres as the master copy

Today Postgres mirrors files (`dual`). The target makes it the only writer
path (`pg`), with these additions that `pgstore.py` does not have yet:

- **A version per document.** `user_docs` gains a `version` integer. A save
  sends the version it read, and the update is `where version = $read`. Zero rows
  means someone else saved first. The request then re-reads, re-applies and
  retries a few times, then fails plainly. This replaces the process-local
  file lock and is the one change that makes several processes safe.
- **Connection pool.** One pool per process with a small cap, instead of one
  connection per thread. Timeouts short, so a slow database degrades a
  request, never hangs a worker.
- **Rows for the things that are not documents.** Sessions, the cost ledger,
  job state and the pending lists become ordinary tables, so "spent today" is
  one indexed `sum`, not a whole-file scan. Stockout reports, friends and
  store maps can follow later (stage 2 in
  `assistant/loops/2026-10-28-supabase-seam.md`); they
  can stay as documents for a long time.
- **Group live sync** keeps `LISTEN/NOTIFY`; with N processes each holds one
  listener, which is already how `live.py` is written.

Migration from JSON, in order, each step reversible:

1. Keep `dual`. Add `version` with a default of 0 and the versioned update
   path behind a flag; files remain the truth. Nothing observable changes.
2. Re-run `assistant/tools/migrate_json_to_pg.py`, compare every document (it reports
   mismatches), and fix any drift. Back up both sides (`backup.sh` already
   dumps the schema when `ARYA_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL` is set).
3. Flip `ARYA_STORE=pg` on one process while the others stay on `dual`
   reads only if the versioned path is on. Otherwise flip the whole site in a
   quiet hour. Keep writing files for a while as a shadow copy (a new
   `pg+shadow` mode, or the same `dual` logic with Postgres first and the file
   second) so rollback is a flag flip, not a restore.
4. Stop the shadow file writes once a full backup cycle has passed with no
   mismatch. From here the files are a backup format, not a store.

Rollback at any step: set `ARYA_STORE` back one mode and redeploy. Before
step 4 the files are current; after step 4 rollback means restore the
latest file export from the database (a small export tool is part of the
phase, see 4).

### 2.3 Session and demo state in a shared store

- **Sign-in sessions** move to a table or the key-value store, keyed by the
  token hash, with the expiry as a TTL. `session_info` reads one key. The
  parsed-file cache (`_SESSIONS_SEEN`) goes away; a short per-process cache
  with a TTL of seconds is fine.
- **Demo sessions and sandboxes** move to the key-value store with a TTL of
  one visit (hours), keyed by the demo cookie. The sandbox overlay is already
  a dict keyed by file path with a 2 MB cap, so it serialises as one value
  per visit. Reads load the overlay once per request; writes save it back at
  the end of the request. This is the change that lets a demo visit survive a
  deploy and lets two processes serve one visitor.
- **Rate-limit and door buckets** move to the same store with atomic
  increments and TTLs, so a cap of "240 door hits per IP per hour" holds
  across processes.
- Keep the in-process path as the fallback when no shared store is set, so
  a laptop run (`compose.yaml`) and the tests stay as they are.

### 2.4 Background jobs and reminders

- Today: one worker thread per process for receipt batches and store scans,
  with a pending list in a file, and a cron line for reminders.
- Target: a queue with named job types (`receipt.read`, `scan.read`,
  `reminders.daily`, `backup.nightly`, `export.account`) and worker processes
  that run the same code as today's thread loops. A job carries the account,
  a lease and a retry count. A crashed worker's lease expires and another
  worker picks the job up. Idempotency keys (the job id plus the frame
  number, which `receiptjobs` already uses) make a retry safe.
- Reminders become a scheduled job that enqueues one `reminders.account` job
  per opted-in account. A slow push to one phone then does not delay the rest,
  and the cron line on the VM goes away.
- The "Your receipts are ready" and "Your map is ready" cards keep polling
  the job list exactly as now; only the producer of that list changes.

### 2.5 Model calls: one gateway, queued, rate-limited

- Every model call already goes through `api/meta_client.py` (and
  `open_client.py` for the open model). The target puts a small gateway
  behind those two modules: a per-model concurrency cap, a per-provider
  token-bucket for the published request limits, retries with backoff on
  429 and 5xx, and a timeout per job kind (Wonder re-reads are long, Ask is
  short).
- Interactive calls (Ask, a single receipt from the camera) keep a reserved
  share of the concurrency so a batch upload never blocks a question.
- Batch calls (bulk receipt reads, scans, judge runs, dictionary enrichment)
  go through the queue (2.4) and the gateway's batch share.
- Budgets stay as they are in policy (`ARYA_DAILY_BUDGET_USD`, demo buckets,
  per-account limits); their counters move to the database (2.2) so they hold
  across processes. A **spend reservation** is taken before the call and
  settled after, so two processes cannot both spend the last dollar.
- The ledger row per call stays the audit record; the gateway writes it.

### 2.6 Caching

Three layers, each safe to lose:

1. **Edge.** The built shell and static images already carry immutable
   cache headers; the CDN serves them. Nothing under `/api/` is cached at
   the edge.
2. **Shared hot cache.** The Today payload per account (and per group plane)
   is cached in the key-value store for a few seconds and dropped on any
   save to that account or group (`save_at` is the one choke point, so the
   invalidation is one line). The same for the price facts and the derived
   list. This is the cheapest win on bottleneck 1 and needs no process
   change; the per-request memo stays as the last layer.
3. **Per-process.** Short TTL caches for sessions and settings.

Rule: cache derived data only. Receipts, lists and flags are read from the
master copy, never from a cache, on a write path.

### 2.7 Object storage for photos

- Receipt originals, shelf frames and map images move to a private bucket,
  one key per account and file (`users/<account>/receipts/<id>.<ext>`),
  with signed, short-lived URLs for "View receipt". The database row keeps
  the key, the size and a content hash.
- `storemap_img.json` stops being one rewritten blob: each image is its own
  object and the map document keeps keys only.
- Uploads keep going through the API (the people-scrubbing step must run
  before anything is stored, as today); the API streams the result to the
  bucket. Deletion of an account deletes its prefix.
- Backups: the bucket has versioning or a nightly copy to a second bucket;
  the database dump is the other half. `restore.sh` restores the volume
  today and would restore the dump plus point at the bucket.

### 2.8 Observability

- **Metrics per process:** request count and latency by route (p50, p95),
  in-flight requests, thread pool queue length, database pool wait, cache
  hit rate, queue depth and job age by type, model calls by model with
  latency, error and 429 counts, spend per bucket. Exposed on a
  `/metrics` endpoint the load balancer does not route to the public.
- **Logs:** one JSON line per request with a request id, account hash (not
  the name), route, status, duration and the job id when one applies. The
  same id goes into model calls and ledger rows.
- **Traces:** optional; a request id in logs covers most of what a trace
  would, until there are several services.
- **Alerts, few and plain:** `/health` red for a few minutes; p95 of
  `/api/today` above a line; queue age above a line; model error rate above
  a line; daily spend near the ceiling. The existing ops digest
  (`harness/ops.py`) becomes a reader of the same metrics.
- **Privacy:** no receipt content, no names and no photos in logs or
  metrics; the people-scrubbing and personal-data rules in `meta_client`
  stay the boundary.

## 3. Phased migration plan

Each phase is turned on by settings on the current image, has a
measurement that says whether it worked, and has a rollback that is a flag
flip or a redeploy of the previous image. Phases go in this order because
each one removes the blocker for the next. None has a date.

| Phase | What changes | Blocker it removes | Rollback | What to measure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0. Baseline | Add request timing and a `/metrics` endpoint; run the Today load script against the live site in a quiet hour; set `ARYA_BACKUP_REMOTE` and prove one restore off the VM | Nothing is known about the live ceiling | Remove the endpoint | p50 and p95 of `/api/today` at 1, 10, 30 concurrent on the live server; restore time |
| 1. Hot cache | Today, price facts and derived list cached per plane for a few seconds, invalidated on save; mirror writes moved off the request path (a background queue in-process, with a circuit breaker on failure) | Bottlenecks 1 (partly), 4 and 7 | Flag off the cache; flag off the async mirror | Same load test: median at 10 and 30 concurrent; cache hit rate; save latency with the mirror slow or down |
| 2. Postgres master | `version` column and versioned updates; connection pool; sessions and ledger as tables; `pg` with shadow file writes; then shadow off | Bottleneck 3 and the one-writer rule | `ARYA_STORE` back one mode; restore from files until shadow is off | Mismatch count from the migration check (must be 0); lost-update retries per hour; database pool wait |
| 3. Shared short-lived state | Demo sessions, sandboxes and rate buckets in a shared key-value store, with the in-process path as fallback | Bottleneck 2 | Unset the store address; the process path returns | A demo visit survives a deploy; door caps hold across two processes |
| 4. Several processes | Start N processes behind the load balancer on the same VM first, then on more than one machine; rolling deploys | Bottleneck 1 | N back to 1 | p50 at 30 concurrent falls in step with N; zero demo visits dropped during a deploy |
| 5. Queue and workers | Receipt, scan and reminder jobs on the queue; worker processes; cron line retired | Bottleneck 5 (partly) | `ARYA_*_JOBS_INLINE` style flags back to the thread loop | Job age p95; retries; jobs lost on a worker restart (must be 0) |
| 6. Model gateway | Concurrency caps, provider rate buckets, spend reservation, interactive reserve | Bottleneck 5 | Caps to unlimited; reservation off | 429s per hour; Ask latency while a batch runs; spend over the ceiling (must be 0) |
| 7. Object storage | Originals, frames and map images in a bucket; `storemap_img.json` split | Bottleneck 6 | Keep files on the volume until the copy is verified; read from the volume on a bucket miss | Bytes on the volume; map save latency; signed-URL errors |
| 8. Cloud provider | Move the whole set (processes, database, store, queue, bucket) to a provider with managed versions of each; the VM becomes a fallback until a full week passes | Hardware ceiling | DNS back to the VM | Same dashboard, same alerts, same load test |

Phases 0 and 1 can happen on the current VM with no new service.
Phase 2 uses the database that already exists. Phase 3 is the first new
service. From phase 4 on, the choice of provider matters, and the design
above lets any of them fit.

## 4. Risks and how the plan answers them

| Risk | Answer |
|---|---|
| Lost updates when two processes save one document | Versioned updates (2.2) before any second process (phase 2 before 4). Never the other order. |
| A migration that silently drops a document | The migration tool already counts mismatches; phase 2 requires zero before `pg`, and shadow file writes keep a second copy. |
| Demo visits dropped during judging | Not a risk here: no phase runs before judging ends. Later, phase 3 removes it. |
| Cost spike from more processes | The budgets are per app, not per process, once counters live in the database (phase 2) and a reservation exists (phase 6). Until then, run one process. |
| Privacy rules weaken as state moves | Each move keeps the same boundary: scrub before store, hashes not names in sessions and logs, personal data only to Meta Standard mode as recorded in `AGENTS.md`. A phase that touches photos (7) needs a privacy review first. |
| Vendor lock-in | Every box is a role with a plain interface (SQL, key-value with TTL, a queue with leases, object keys with signed URLs). Nothing uses a provider-only feature. |
| More moving parts than one person can run | Each phase stays optional and off by default; a laptop run and the tests keep the in-process path. The dashboard and alerts (2.8) come in phase 0, before anything else. |
| Reads stay slow because the engines are Python | The hot cache (phase 1) and N processes (phase 4) are the first answers. Precomputing the derived state on save instead of on read is a later option the memo design already allows. |

## 5. What stays the same

The product rules, the engines in code at $0, the one model client, the
cost policy, the privacy boundary, the PWA, the connector and the API. A
shopper would not see a phase happen, except that Today loads as fast with
hundreds of neighbours as it does alone today.

## 6. Related pages

- [`ROADMAP.md`](/docs/roadmap): the one-line plan this page expands.
- [`../README.md#what-are-the-known-limits`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md#what-are-the-known-limits): the limit as
  judges read it.
- [`../assistant/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](/docs/architecture/overview):
  what runs today, section by section.
- [`../assistant/docs/SCALE-SIM.md`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/assistant/docs/SCALE-SIM.md): the
  simulator and its earlier findings.
- `assistant/docs/OPS.md`: the runbook that each phase updates.
