<!-- https://docs.arya.teamnightshift.org/docs/api/lists-api -->

# Arya Lists API v1

Read and write your own Arya lists from another app or a script, and take
your data with you. The same personal API token that the agent connector
uses works here. Make one in Arya under Settings › Use Arya in another AI
app. The code shows once; a new code replaces it.

Base URL: `https://arya.teamnightshift.org/api/v1`

The same guide, shorter, is the public page at `/developers`, with a
five-minute quickstart in curl, Python and JavaScript. The interactive
reference (try the calls from the browser) is at `/developers/reference`.

`/api/v1` is frozen. Changes after it ships are additive only: new
endpoints, new optional fields, new response fields. Clients must ignore
fields they do not know. The machine-readable schema is at
`/api/v1/openapi.json` (public, no token needed).

```bash
export ARYA=https://arya.teamnightshift.org/api/v1
export TOKEN=...   # your code
```

Every call sends `Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN`. The token reaches only
your own account's data. Cookie sign-in does not work on `/api/v1`.

## Lists and items

A list is `{id, name, stores, open_count}`. `open_count` is the number of
items not yet checked. The id `unfiled` is "Everything else": the items
that sit on no named list. An item is
`{id, name, qty, unit, checked, aisle, added_at, list_id}`.

- `aisle` is the department you set yourself, else `null`. Arya's own
  guess from the name is not part of the API.
- `added_at` is a UTC time. It is `null` for items added before the API
  existed and for items Arya suggested.
- `checked` is for the current shopping cycle, as in the app.
- An item sits on one list at a time.

### GET /lists

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $ARYA/lists
# [{"id":"unfiled","name":"Everything else","stores":[],"open_count":1},
#  {"id":"l-1a2b3c4d","name":"Costco","stores":["Costco"],"open_count":3}]
```

### GET /lists/{id}

The list, plus `items`.

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $ARYA/lists/l-1a2b3c4d
```

### POST /lists/{id}/items

Add items. Send `items` (structured) or `text` (free text), not both.
At most 50 items per call.

```bash
# structured: a name, or an object with qty, unit and aisle
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"items":["oat milk",{"name":"rice","qty":2,"unit":"kg","aisle":"Pantry"}]}' \
  $ARYA/lists/l-1a2b3c4d/items

# free text: split the way the app splits typed lists ("eggs x 3, bread")
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text":"milk\neggs x 3\nbread"}' $ARYA/lists/l-1a2b3c4d/items
```

Reply:

```json
{"added": 2, "already": 1, "already_names": [{"name": "milk", "list": "Costco"}],
 "also_on": [], "skipped": [], "items": [ ... ]}
```

- `already`: names that were already on this list. They are not added twice.
- `also_on`: names that are already on a **different** list. The API does
  not move them and does not add them to this list; the reply says where
  they are. To move one, `PATCH` its `list_id`. (In the app a person can
  keep an item on more than one list. The API shows such an item once, under
  its main list, and its ticks there are the main list's.)
- `skipped`: pieces of `text` that were not items (a bare number). A line with a sentence in it is skipped whole, so no piece of it is added.
- `items`: the items now on the list for the names you sent.
- `text` is split by fixed rules. The API makes no model calls.

### PATCH /items/{id}

Change any of `checked`, `qty`, `unit`, `list_id` (a list id, `unfiled`, or
`null` for Everything else), `aisle` (`""` clears it).
Nothing changes if any field is bad.

```bash
curl -s -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"checked":true}' $ARYA/items/manual-milk
curl -s -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"list_id":"l-9f8e7d6c","qty":2,"aisle":"Dairy"}' $ARYA/items/manual-milk
```

Reply: the item.

### DELETE /items/{id}

```bash
curl -s -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $ARYA/items/manual-milk
# {"deleted":"manual-milk"}
```

## Export and import

### GET /lists/{id}/export?format=csv|json|text

`json` (the default) is `{"list": {id, name, stores}, "items": [...]}`.
`text` is a checklist, one item per line: `☐ rice 2 kg`, `☐ eggs x 12`,
`☑ milk`. `csv` has this header and these columns, in this order:

```text
name,qty,unit,checked,department,list
rice,2,kg,false,Pantry,Costco
```

`checked` is `true` or `false`. A cell that starts with `= + - @` gets a
leading apostrophe so a spreadsheet does not run it as a formula. Import
removes it.

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$ARYA/lists/l-1a2b3c4d/export?format=csv" > costco.csv
```

### POST /lists/import

Send the file as the request body. The format is `csv` when the
`Content-Type` contains `csv`, else `text`. `?format=csv|text` overrides that.
`?list=Name` is the list to fill (default `Imported`). It is created if you
do not have it; names match without regard to case. In a CSV, a `list`
column per row wins over `?list=`. Only `name` is required in a CSV. A
text body takes the checklist lines above or any plain list. At most 500
rows.

```bash
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: text/csv" \
  --data-binary @costco.csv "$ARYA/lists/import?list=Costco"
# {"created":3,"skipped":0,"lists":[{"id":"l-1a2b3c4d","name":"Costco"}]}
```

`created` is the number of new items. `skipped` counts rows that were
empty, not items, repeated, over the 500 limit, or already on a list.
Checked state and department are applied to new items only.

## Your receipts and totals

Your own data only: the receipts **you** filed. Receipts filed by other
members of your household group are not returned. Nothing here is
inferred by Arya. Totals are sums of what your receipts say.

A receipt is `{id, merchant, date, total, subtotal, tax, items, reconciles,
has_photo}`. The detail adds `lines`: `{name, qty, unit_price, line_total,
line_type}` with `line_type` `item`, `discount` or `return` (returns are
negative).

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$ARYA/receipts?limit=20&offset=0"   # newest first, max 200
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $ARYA/receipts/ext-1a2b3c4d5e
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $ARYA/receipts/ext-1a2b3c4d5e/original > receipt.jpg
curl -s -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $ARYA/receipts/ext-1a2b3c4d5e
```

`GET /receipts/export?format=csv|json` returns every receipt you filed.
The CSV has one row per line, with columns
`receipt_id,merchant,date,name,qty,unit_price,line_total,line_type`.

`/receipts/{id}/original` is the photo or PDF you uploaded, if Arya kept one
(`has_photo`). Filing a receipt through the API is not in v1; use the app
or the agent connector.

### GET /analysis/spending

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $ARYA/analysis/spending
# {"trips":2,"spend_total":11.5,"returns_total":4.0,
#  "by_month":{"2026-10":11.5},"by_store":{"Costco":11.5,"Trader Joe's":0.0}}
```

`spend_total` adds up the receipt totals. `by_store` groups by the merchant
name printed on the receipt.

### GET /analysis/purchases?limit=50

What you bought and when, by the name Arya read from the receipt (max 500):
`{"items":[{"name","times_bought","qty","spent","first_bought","last_bought"}]}`,
most often bought first. Returns and discounts are not counted as buys.

## Errors

Errors are JSON, with the matching HTTP status:

```json
{"error": {"code": "not_found", "message": "no such list"}}
```

| Status | `code` | When |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `bad_request` | a bad or unknown field, bad JSON, bad format |
| 401 | `unauthorized` | no token, a wrong token, or a revoked token |
| 404 | `not_found` | no such list or item (also for another account's ids) |
| 413 | `too_large` | body over 256 KB |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | over the hourly limit; see `Retry-After` |
| 500 | `internal_error` | our fault; try again |

## Limits

- 600 calls per account per hour, shared with the agent connector and
  every other route a token reaches (`ARYA_MCP_RATE`). Over it you get `429` with a `Retry-After` header
  in seconds.
- 256 KB per request, 50 items per add call, 500 rows per import.

## Later

Not in v1: webhooks, OAuth, sharing a list with another account, filing a
receipt, and Quest data. Arya's own inference (what is running low,
suggestions, aisle and store maps, prices from other households) is not
part of the API on purpose. The API is for your own data.

---

<!-- https://docs.arya.teamnightshift.org/docs/roadmap -->

# After the hackathon

These are ideas for where Arya could go. They are not commitments, and I
need more time to work them out.

**What ships now is a limited-scope MVP:** Arya learns from receipts,
Ask, groups, Quest and the connector, as described in the README and
`STATUS.md`. **This page is what could come later.** Nothing on it is built
unless it says so, and nothing is promised for the submission. "Idea" means
nobody has designed it yet. Sources are named so you can check them.

## Devices
- **Native iOS and Android apps; the PWA stays.** Plan. The PWA was the
  fastest way to build in a hackathon. Not designed or scheduled, and not in
  any app store today.
- **Ray-Ban Meta glasses.** Idea, raised by me for the store scan.
  Spark's check during the hackathon found no public live-camera API for
  third-party apps. The flow that works today is to capture on the glasses,
  sync to the phone and import the video there. The demo uses the phone camera
  throughout. Source: `docs/quest/DISCUSSION.md` (item 38).
- **Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses.** Idea. Not researched yet. What is possible
  depends on what Meta offers developers for that device.

## Store data and community
- **Capture more store data.** Item-level locations from scan captures,
  reports that close themselves, flags that expire when nobody confirms them,
  and mapping quietly from Find it for me frames. Source:
  `docs/quest/MAP-MY-STORE.md`, "Not built yet".
- **Arya shoppers and community prices.** Opt-in prices, deals and live
  presence (Quiet, Busy, Packed). Today the opt-in records a choice only. A
  community figure would need 5 or more households over 30 days, a median and
  no names. Source: `assistant/docs/SPEC.md` (FR-11.7), `assistant/docs/SCALE-SIM.md`.
- **Quest community layer.** Leaderboards, badges the data makes funny, team
  Shop-Offs settled by receipt time and Clue Hunts. Designed, not built.
  Source: `docs/quest/GAME-DESIGN.md`.
- **A store-data partnership.** Online store videos are off limits (copyright,
  platform terms). A licensed source of in-store video and photos could power
  better maps. See [`docs/MODELS.md`](/docs/architecture/models).
- **Density first.** Cover one metro's stores completely before expanding. A thin
  layer over many stores is worth little. Source: `docs/quest/BUSINESS.md`.
- **Store maps at scale.** Maps already merge across shoppers. Not built:
  resolving conflicts between maps. Source: `assistant/docs/SPEC.md`, "Not in scope".
- **Shared lists, further.** Not built: split lists inside a group, and sharing a
  list with another account through the API (`docs/API.md`, "Later").
- Item and store profile pages; split the list (kids or a partner); friend run
  notifications (designed, not built); reimbursement tracking for items bought
  for others.
- Invite links work today (`/?join=CODE` opens Join a group). Ideas for growth
  as a community product, none designed: shared recipe or meal lists, and a
  public page for a store's map status.

## AI and open weights
- **Bring your own Meta key.** Decided against for now. The code is in the repo,
  unfinished and switched off (see "Use your own Meta key" below).
- **Replay mode** (recorded answers, so the AI parts work without a key).
  Planned, not built.
- **More use of open weights.** Muse Spark Open is a second seat on the staple
  judge and labels dictionary names today. Wider use would need the personal
  data rule kept (names only).
- **More languages.** Ask answers in the language you write. Spanish and Hindi
  were the ones verified. The app's buttons and labels are English only
  (`assistant/docs/MULTILINGUAL-ASK.md`). Translating the app itself is a separate project.
- **A hosted open-weights option.** Today one open model (Muse Spark Open) is
  hosted on Baseten for two small jobs. A fuller option for people who want
  their reads on open weights is an idea only.
- **Models we did not use** (Spark Contributor for a community tier, Muse
  Glimmer self-hosted): see [`docs/MODELS.md`](/docs/architecture/models).
- A non-English Ask currently sends the whole feature guide (about 19 KB) on
  each question. Trimming that is planned.

## Trust and privacy
- A photo opt-in and a full privacy policy; store permission for mapping.
  Source: `docs/quest/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- Security review items that were deferred, tracked as GitHub issues.
- A community tier with user opt-in is an idea only
  (`assistant/docs/MODEL-POLICY.md`).
- The forgot-password flow is held, by choice
  (`assistant/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, section 13, "Not built / held").
- Arya's own code is MIT licensed (`LICENSE`). The Meta models and third-party
  code keep their own terms (`NOTICE.md`).

## Running it yourself
- More for self-hosters: a one-command setup for a small server with TLS (the
  laptop setup is in `docs/RUN-IT-YOURSELF.md`).
- Off-site backups with rclone (`ARYA_BACKUP_REMOTE` exists; no bucket is set
  up) and a staging address to check a deploy before the live one.
- Cost proposals from the cost watcher, tracked as GitHub issues.
- **Scale out as the community grows.** Today Arya is one server process on
  one VM (see [Known limits](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/README.md#what-are-the-known-limits)). The plan, not a
  promise: make Postgres the master copy, move demo and session state out of
  memory, run several processes, and move to a cloud provider in step with
  the number of shoppers. The design, phase by
  phase, is in [`SCALABILITY-DESIGN.md`](/docs/architecture/scalability) (a plan,
  not built).

## Developer platform and integrations
The starting point today is the Lists API and the developer portal at `/developers`
(with a quickstart and an interactive reference; `docs/API.md`), plus the MCP
connector that lets an AI agent read and edit your lists
(`assistant/docs/AGENT-CONNECTOR.md`). The API is for your own data, with a
personal token. Desk research on who else is in this space, with its unverified
claims flagged, is in [`MARKET.md`](https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya/blob/main/docs/MARKET.md). Everything below is future work
and not built:
- **A bigger developer portal,** so other platforms can connect to Arya,
  with Arya's household data as the shared source. That means more endpoints (receipts,
  spend, what is running low), webhooks, OAuth sign-in instead of a personal
  token, SDKs and sample apps.
- **Smart fridges, cooking devices and home robots** that add what is empty
  or expiring to the list and feed back what was used.
- **Online grocery delivery services and apps,** to send a list for ordering
  and to bring back the real receipt and prices. (There is no cart or payment in
  Arya today; see `assistant/docs/SPEC.md`, "Not in scope".)
- **Any app that understands a household's food and purchase habits** (meal
  planners, nutrition and budgeting apps), connected through the same API and
  the import and export below.
- Every integration would be opt-in, per household, with scoped permissions
  and a clear way to revoke it.

## Spending, import and export
- **Richer spend tracking and analysis,** with filters (by store, category,
  person, period, price per unit). The Spending screen exists today; deeper
  analysis and filters are not built.
- **Export to other budgeting apps** (spend and receipts as CSV or a direct
  connection). Today the API lists your own data (`docs/API.md`); a budgeting
  export is not built.
- **Import lists from other list apps** (a file or a link). Not built.

## More ideas for growing the app and its community
All of these are ideas. None is designed or built. Each would need my go-ahead
and, where it touches personal data, a privacy review first.

**Everyday use**
- Meal planning from what is running low and what to use soon, with a
  shopping list built from the plan.
- **Recipe to shopping list, then to stores.** Turn a recipe (link, photo or
  typed) into list items, then use the household's receipt history to suggest
  where and which brand to buy. Not built.
- Budget goals per store or per month on the Spending screen, with a gentle
  heads-up and never a lock.
- Barcode scan to add an item or check a price against your own history.
- Pantry and fridge check-in by photo (outside the current spec).
- Home Screen widgets and watch glances for the list and for use-soon items.
- Calendar-aware reminders, such as "you host on Saturday".
- Voice assistants (Siri, Google Assistant) adding to the list (Alexa is built
  but switched off, see below), and
  more connectors beyond the Muse agent and MCP.
- Receipt import from email or a store account, so no photo is needed.
- Warranty and return reminders read from receipts (Return Regret already
  shows returns are tracked).
- Waste tracking and a monthly "what we threw away" view.
- Gift and event lists with a shared link and no account needed to view.
- Accessibility: a screen-reader review and a calmer Quest mode. (Text size
  and spacing already exist in Settings, under Display.)

**Community**
- Neighborhood and store pages with shared tips, labelled as opt-in.
- Verified store news from shoppers, expiring when nobody confirms it.
- Seasonal Quest events, themed skins (escape room) and household leaderboards
  that stay private by default.
- A mapper reputation and thanks for people who map stores, with no pay
  attached.
- Clubs and teams (families, roommates, offices, school pantries, food banks).
- A public gallery of store maps that are fresh and photo-backed.
- Shared price alerts when a household opts in to share a figure.

**AI and open weights**
- A hosted open-weights reader for receipts, for people who want that choice.
- A smaller on-device model for offline add and quick matches.
- Better product merge and split suggestions in the Curator, and learned
  substitutions (the usual brand when one is out of stock).
- Ask Arya acting on more things, with a confirm step for anything that
  changes data.
- A public set of evals so others can check the reader scores.

**Trust, privacy and operating it**
- One place for privacy controls. Export my data and Delete my account already
  exist in Settings, under Account. The idea is to gather them with the other
  privacy choices.
- A public status page and an uptime history.
- A staging address, and automated CI instead of manual runs.
- A published API with webhooks and OAuth (`docs/API.md`, "Later").
- Store permission programme for mapping, and a takedown route for stores.

## Alexa skill: built, switched off, not tested on a device
The code is merged (#515 and #516) behind the `ARYA_ALEXA` flag, which is off in
the live app and the demo. I paused it until after the hackathon. It adds items
by voice only and has not been tried on a real Echo. Amazon has retired its Alexa
list API, so Arya cannot sync with Alexa's own lists.

## Use your own Meta key: unfinished, switched off, not used
The code exists (PRs #391 and #393), it is unfinished, and it is switched off
in the live app and the demo. I decided on 2026-11-02 not to use it. Operator
notes: `assistant/docs/OPS.md`, "Own Meta keys (BYOK)".
